title: What a language model computes
summary: A language model turns the tokens so far into a probability for every token that could come next. Everything a chat product shows you is that loop, plus a sampler, plus a contract about messages. This room builds that picture so later rooms on retrieval, tools, and voice have somewhere to attach.

blocks.title: Verification
blocks.text: Source note: last-verified was left unmarked until a person checks the cited pages. The citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date.

A language model turns the tokens so far into a probability for every token that could come next. Everything a chat product shows you is that loop, plus a sampler, plus a contract about messages. This room builds that picture so later rooms on retrieval, tools, and voice have somewhere to attach.
01Executive summary

items: At inference, the model does not “look up an answer.” It scores possible next tokens. A sampler picks one, the token is appended, and the score runs again until a stop condition.

The 2017 Transformer computes those scores with attention: each position mixes information from other positions using queries, keys, and values, scaled by the square root of the key dimension, then passed through a feed-forward network. Residuals and layer normalization wrap each sub-layer. [cite:1]

Sampling is a separate choice from the network. Temperature reshapes the distribution. Nucleus (top-p) sampling keeps the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p. OpenAI documents temperature on a 0–2 scale and asks you not to change temperature and top-p together. [cite:2] [cite:4]

An API adds a message list, an instruction channel, usage counts, and a finish reason. OpenAI’s text-generation guide recommends the Responses API for new text work and warns that the output array is not “the string at index zero.” [cite:3]

Embeddings are a different product from the hidden states inside the chat model. OpenAI’s embedding guide gives default widths of 1536 and 3072 for two third-generation models and recommends cosine similarity. Do not reuse those vectors as if they were the model’s internal residual stream. [cite:5]

blocks.title: Why it matters for the lab engineer
blocks.text: Interviewers ask this room in disguise: “what is a token,” “why did the model hallucinate,” “what does temperature do,” “where would you put a knowledge base.” Contact-center work asks the same questions with a caller on the line. If you can draw the path from audio transcript to next token to spoken reply, you can debug a voice bot without blaming “the AI.” The rooms on RAG and MCP assume this picture. They do not replace it.
02Architecture
Primary path. Numbers match the walk-through in the next sections. The SVG is the phase-0 diagram; Studio may repaint it.
Diagram: Seven stages: text, tokens, embed plus position, blocks, logits, sample, text

items: 1–2 are your string and the tokenizer. They are not the neural net.
3–5 are the network: vectors in, a logit per vocabulary token out.
6 is the sampler. Temperature lives here, not inside attention.
7 writes text the user sees. A stop, a tool call, or a length cap can end the loop earlier.

flowchart LR
  A["1 Text"] --> B["2 Token ids"]
  B --> C["3 Embed + position"]
  C --> D["4 Blocks: attention then feed-forward"]
  D --> E["5 Logits"]
  E --> F["6 Sample"]
  F --> G["7 Detokenize"]

The dotted return is the loop. One forward pass produces one new token (or, on some serving stacks, a small draft). The weights do not change during that loop. Learning happened earlier, on another machine, and is outside this diagram. Whether a given model is dense or a mixture of experts is a model-card fact. Meta’s Llama 4 card, fetched 2026-10-14, describes Scout and Maverick as auto-regressive mixture-of-experts models with early fusion, natively multimodal. Scout is 17 billion activated parameters, 109 billion total, 16 experts. Maverick is 17 billion activated, 400 billion total, 128 experts. The OpenAI models page fetched the same day does not publish depth, width, or a block diagram for gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, or gpt-6-luna. Draw the extras the card draws, and stop there. [cite:20] [cite:10]
03Deep dive

Start from the object the API actually returns: a continuation. You sent text, wrapped as messages. You received text, plus metadata. Between those two strings the provider ran a tokenizer, a network whose parameters are fixed for the call, and a sampler. If you remember only one sentence, remember that the network’s immediate output is a vector of scores over the vocabulary, not a paragraph.

The 2017 Transformer paper is the architecture this lab uses as the foundation, and it is an encoder–decoder built only from attention. The authors dispense with recurrence and convolution. In the configuration they specify, the encoder is a stack of N = 6 identical layers and the decoder is a stack of N = 6 as well. Each encoder layer has two sub-layers: multi-head self-attention, then a position-wise feed-forward network. Around each sub-layer they put a residual connection and layer normalization, written LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)). The model dimension they use for that design is d_model = 512, so the residual add is legal. The decoder adds a third sub-layer that attends over the encoder, and it masks the self-attention so position i cannot see future positions. That mask, plus output embeddings offset by one, is what makes the prediction depend only on tokens already known. [cite:1]

Those numbers (6 layers, width 512) describe the paper’s base layout, not a model you can buy in 2026. Treat them as the diagram’s legend. As of 2026-10-14, OpenAI’s models page lists a 1.05M-token context window and a 128K max output for gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, and gpt-6-luna. That page does not publish layer count or hidden width, so those stay off this diagram. [cite:10] The BLEU scores in the paper — 28.4 on WMT 2014 English-to-German and 41.0 on English-to-French, the big model trained for 3.5 days on eight GPUs — are historical results. They are not a claim about current translation quality. [cite:1]
Three places a fact can live
When an answer is wrong, the first diagnostic cut is where the fact was supposed to come from. Mixing these up is the usual reason a team “tunes temperature” for a problem that is a missing document.

rows: The weights. The 2020 RAG paper calls this parametric memory: knowledge stored in the network. [cite:7]
Training or a fine-tune. Not during a normal API call.
The fact was never in the training mixture, or it changed after training. The model still emits fluent text.
The tokens inside this request: instructions, messages, and anything you pasted, including retrieved chunks.
Every request. This is the lever prompting and RAG share.
The fact was in the window but the sampler or the instruction ignored it, or it was truncated before the call.

Systems outside the forward pass. A vector index is the non-parametric memory in the RAG paper: an index you can replace. [cite:7] A tool is a function the model may request; you execute it. That split is T4.
When you update the index or the tool, without editing weights.
The call never happened, the filter excluded the row, or the result was not fed back into the next forward pass.

blocks.text: Tokens, vectors, scores
People say “embedding” for three different vectors. The table is the antidote. Only one of them belongs in a vector database.

rows: An integer in the tokenizer’s vocabulary.
Counting cost, spotting a truncated word, debugging a weird character. Not a distance.
A vector of width d_model. In the 2017 model, token embeddings and the pre-softmax projection share weights, and the embedding is scaled by the square root of d_model. [cite:1]
The embedding table inside the language model.
Understanding the paper. This room does not claim that a chat endpoint returns that vector.

A vector added to the token embedding. The paper uses sinusoids of geometric wavelengths, and reports that learned positional embeddings scored nearly the same in their setup. They chose sinusoids because a fixed offset might be a linear function of the base encoding, which they hoped would help the model extrapolate past the trained length. [cite:1]
Added because a pure attention stack has no recurrence and no convolution, so order would otherwise be invisible. [cite:1]

Remembering why “bag of tokens” is not this architecture. Meta’s Llama 4 blog, fetched 2026-10-14, names iRoPE: interleaved attention layers without positional embeddings, RoPE on most layers, and inference-time temperature scaling of attention. The OpenAI models page fetched the same day does not name a positional scheme. [cite:21] [cite:10]
One real number per vocabulary token, before softmax.
The last linear layer of the network.
The input to sampling. Log probabilities of the chosen tokens are optional API output. [cite:4]
A distribution over positions for one query. After scaling and softmax, the weights multiply the values. [cite:1]
Explanation of mixing. A single head’s map is not “the reason” the model said a sentence. This room does not treat an attention viewer as a faithful explanation.

A vector from an embedding model, not from the chat model’s residual stream. OpenAI documents default length 1536 for `text-embedding-3-small` and 3072 for `text-embedding-3-large`, and a `dimensions` parameter to shorten third-generation vectors. [cite:5]
Nearest-neighbor search. Cosine similarity is what that guide recommends. The choice of distance “typically doesn’t matter much,” in their words. [cite:5]

blocks.text: What happens at training time versus call time
You do not need the training recipe to use the API. You do need the split, because fine-tuning (T6) is a deliberate return to training, and an ordinary request is not.

rows: Updated to predict tokens on a large corpus.
The result is a next-token model. The Transformer’s training objective in the machine-translation setup is sequence transduction, not “store this wiki page.” [cite:1]

Corpus and context, where a card states them. Llama 4 Scout: about 40 trillion tokens, context length 10 million, knowledge cutoff August 2024. Maverick: about 22 trillion tokens, context length 1 million, the same cutoff. The Meta blog says Scout was pre-trained and post-trained with a 256 thousand-token context, which empowers length generalization, and it names a supported context of 10 million tokens. The OpenAI models page does not publish a corpus size. [cite:20] [cite:21]

This room does not teach the algorithm. T6 does. Provider marketing names are not a spec.

The Llama 4 card distinguishes instruction-tuned models, for assistant-like chat and visual reasoning, from pretrained models that can be adapted for natural-language generation. It does not name a preference method such as RLHF or DPO. That absence is the fetched finding. It is not a claim that no preference step happened. [cite:20]

You pay for tokens processed and tokens generated. As of 2026-10-14, OpenAI’s pricing page lists standard short-context rates (≤272K input tokens) per 1M tokens: gpt-6-astra $10 input / $50 output, gpt-6.1-sol $2 / $10, gpt-4o-mini $0.15 / $0.60. Long-context columns are higher on that page. Re-fetch before you invoice. [cite:9]

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: When you explain a model to a senior engineer, separate the network from the sampler in the first minute. Temperature does not “make attention softer.” It changes how the next id is drawn from the distribution the network already produced. If the fact was absent from both the weights and the context, no temperature will fetch it.

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: OpenAI’s chat-completions reference says to alter temperature or top_p, not both. Both knobs reshape the same distribution. Turning them at once makes a regression impossible to read. The documented temperature range on that endpoint is 0 to 2. Higher values such as 0.8 are described as more random; lower values such as 0.2 as more focused. [cite:4] The fetched chat-completions page documents the range 0 to 2. It does not say that 0 is greedy argmax. This room does not claim that it is.
Worked example: softmax, then temperature

This arithmetic is a teaching example. It is not the output of a product model. Softmax turns logits into probabilities that sum to 1. Subtracting the max logit before the exponential is the stable way to compute it and does not change the result.

Take three candidate tokens with logits 2, 1, and 0. Subtract 2. The shifted logits are 0, −1, and −2. The exponentials are about 1, 0.3679, and 0.1353. Their sum is about 1.5032. The probabilities are about 0.665, 0.245, and 0.090. The mode holds about two thirds of the mass. The tail is small but not empty.

A common definition of temperature T is to divide the logits by T before softmax. At T = 0.5 the logits become 4, 2, and 0. Exponentials are about 54.60, 7.389, and 1. The sum is about 62.99. Probabilities are about 0.867, 0.117, and 0.016. The distribution got sharper, which matches the docs’ description of lower temperature as more focused. [cite:4] At T = 2 the same logits become 1, 0.5, and 0. Exponentials are about 2.718, 1.649, and 1. The sum is about 5.367. Probabilities are about 0.507, 0.307, and 0.186. The tail grew. That is the whole mechanism. Nothing in the attention block moved.
Teaching chart for logits 2, 1, 0. Bar length is probability, not a benchmark.
Each row shows only the top token’s probability so you can see the mode shrink as temperature rises. The other two tokens take the rest.
Worked example: one query, two keys

Scaled dot-product attention is the formula in the paper: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q K transpose / sqrt(d_k)) V. The scale exists because if the components of a query and a key are independent with mean 0 and variance 1, their dot product has variance d_k, and large magnitudes push softmax into a flat-gradient region. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) counters that. [cite:1]

Teaching numbers, not a trained head. Let d_k = 2 so sqrt(d_k) is about 1.414. One query q = [1, 0]. Two keys: k1 = [1, 0] and k2 = [0, 1]. Dot products are 1 and 0. Scaled scores are about 0.707 and 0. Exponentials are about 2.028 and 1. Softmax weights are about 0.670 and 0.330. If the values are vectors v1 and v2, the output is 0.670 v1 + 0.330 v2. The query mostly copies the value that matched it, and still leaks a third of the other value. Masking, in the decoder, would set a disallowed score to negative infinity before softmax so its weight becomes zero. [cite:1]

Multi-head attention runs several of these projections and concatenates. The paper uses multi-head attention in three places: encoder self-attention, decoder self-attention with the causal mask, and decoder–encoder attention. [cite:1] A chat model you call may only expose the decoder side of that idea. Neither the OpenAI models page nor the Llama 4 card publishes a Vaswani-style encoder–decoder layer diagram. The Llama 4 card says the models are auto-regressive mixture-of-experts with early fusion. [cite:10] [cite:20]
Nucleus sampling, beside temperature

Holtzman and co-authors define nucleus (top-p) sampling as drawing from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds a threshold p. The set grows and shrinks with the shape of the distribution at that step. The point of the paper is to cut an unreliable tail without freezing the candidate count the way a fixed top-k does. [cite:2]

Apply that definition to the T = 1 example, probabilities 0.665, 0.245, 0.090, already sorted. If p = 0.9, the first token’s mass is 0.665, which is under 0.9. Adding the second reaches about 0.910, which clears 0.9. The nucleus is the first two tokens. The third is discarded, and you renormalize over the two that remain. If p = 0.5, the first token alone already exceeds 0.5, so the nucleus is one token. That is not the same operation as temperature. Temperature rewrote every logit. Nucleus deleted a tail and renormalized.

OpenAI’s parameter `top_p` is documented as this idea: the model considers tokens within the top_p probability mass, and 0.1 means the tokens comprising the top 10 percent of mass. [cite:4] Keep the paper’s “smallest set whose cumulative mass exceeds p” and the vendor’s wording next to each other when you implement. If they ever diverge for a model, the vendor’s API reference is what your code must obey, and the paper is what you cite for the idea. [cite:2]
What the message API adds

The network does not know it is in a “system” role. The provider’s serving stack turns roles into the token sequence the network sees, using a template you often do not control. OpenAI’s text-generation guide says the `instructions` parameter is the place for tone, goals, and examples of correct behavior, and that instructions given that way take priority over a prompt placed in `input`. [cite:3] The same guide says an output array often holds more than one item — tool calls, reasoning-token data, and other objects — and that it is not safe to assume the text lives at `output[0]`. Official SDKs may expose a convenience property that concatenates text. [cite:3]

The chat-completions reference, which the guide calls the older API, still documents `logprobs` as a boolean. When true, the response includes the log probability of each output token in the message content. `top_logprobs` is an integer from 0 to 20 and requires `logprobs` true; it asks for the most likely tokens at each position, and the service may return fewer than you asked. [cite:4] Log probabilities are how you notice the model was unsure. They are not a truth score. A confident wrong token is a high probability on the wrong id.

Remember four habits. A model id on a vendor page goes stale, and the habit does not: use the text API the current guide recommends, pin a dated snapshot, keep the prompt in the repo, and do not read the reply from a fixed index. OpenAI’s text generation guide, retrieved 2026-10-14, prints the sentences this room is willing to repeat. The strings `gpt-6-astra` and `gpt-5.5-2026-04-23` appear inside those sentences as the page’s own examples. They are not a recommendation from this lab, and they are not a promise that your key can call them. [cite:3]

blocks.title: Quoted from the text guide, retrieved 2026-10-14
blocks.text: If you're building any text generation app, we recommend using the Responses API over the older Chat Completions API.

Reasoning models, like `gpt-6-astra`, behave differently from chat models and respond better to different prompts. One important note is that reasoning models perform better and demonstrate higher intelligence when used with the Responses API.
Pinning your production applications to specific model snapshots (like `gpt-5.5-2026-04-23` for example) to ensure consistent behavior
OpenAI is deprecating reusable prompt objects in the API. Prompt creation will be de-emphasized beginning June 3, 2026, and `v1/prompts` is scheduled to shut down on November 30, 2026.
It is not safe to assume that the model's text output is present at `output[0].content[0].text`.

Note that the `instructions` parameter only applies to the current response generation request. If you are managing conversation state with the `previous_response_id` parameter, the `instructions` used on previous turns will not be present in the context.

The first sentence is the API choice. The second compares reasoning models with chat models, and the id in it is also the id in the page’s code samples (`model: "gpt-6-astra"`). Copy whatever id the page shows on the day you build, then pin a snapshot the way the third sentence describes. The snapshot inside the parentheses is their example of a pin, not a model this lab has called. The fourth sentence is why the prompt lives in git, on the dates the page prints: June 3, 2026, and November 30, 2026. The fifth is why a playground reply can look empty in your client. Walk the output items, or use the SDK property `output_text`. The last sentence is why a continued conversation still needs the instruction resent. [cite:3] [cite:4]

blocks.text: Certifications are not how this room is graded. Current names, fetched 2026-10-14, live on the Start here page: AWS Certified AI Practitioner, AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer – Associate, Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate (Microsoft’s Azure AI Engineer Associate page says that certification and its renewal assessment are retired), and Google Professional Machine Learning Engineer. [cite:24] [cite:25] [cite:26] [cite:27] The skill this room trains is the explanation, which any of those exams will ask in plainer clothes: what the model computes, what you control at request time, and what you must not pretend the weights contain.
04Walk-through
One completion. Actors are the application, the HTTP API, the tokenizer, the network, and the sampler. Steps match the table.
Diagram: Sequence from the application through the API, tokenizer, network, and sampler

Walk a single user message, “Summarize the outage in one sentence,” with a system instruction that says to abstain if the outage is not in the thread. No retrieval in this room. The interesting part is what is absent: no document, so abstention has to come from the instruction and from the model’s willingness to follow it, not from a search miss.

rows: Messages, model id, sampling knobs, optional logprobs
Put stable instructions in the channel the guide says takes priority. Do not also crank temperature and top_p.
The rendered prompt string, including whatever special tokens the template adds
Role labels become tokens. The template is provider-owned. This room does not name the template for a model id.

A word is often several ids. Cost and context limits count ids, not words. The embedding endpoint documents 8192 input tokens as the per-input max for its models; chat limits are a different number. OpenAI’s models page, fetched 2026-10-14, lists a 1.05 million-token context and a 128 thousand-token max output for gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, and gpt-6-luna. The Llama 4 card lists a 10 million-token context for Scout and a 1 million-token context for Maverick. [cite:10] [cite:20]
Embeddings plus position, then masked attention and a feed-forward sub-layer per block
Causal mask: a new position may attend only to positions up to itself. [cite:1] Weights stay frozen.
This vector is the model’s whole opinion about the next id.
One chosen id, appended, until stop
Temperature and nucleus apply here. [cite:2] Stop can be a stop string, a length cap, or a tool-call shape. Tool calls are T4.
Detokenization can join pieces with spaces the user did not expect. Inspect the raw string when punctuation looks wrong.
Text, finish reason, token usage, optional logprobs

Do not read text from a fixed index if you are on the Responses API. [cite:3] Usage is your cost meter. As of 2026-10-14, OpenAI’s pricing page lists standard short-context rates (≤272K input tokens) per 1M tokens: gpt-6-astra $10 input / $50 output, gpt-6.1-sol $2 / $10, gpt-4o-mini $0.15 / $0.60. Long-context columns are higher on that page. [cite:9]

blocks.text: If step 4 never saw the outage, step 6 can still emit a fluent sentence. That sentence is a sample from a distribution, not a retrieved record. The fix is to put the outage in context (T3) or to refuse when it is absent (instruction plus an eval), not to “ask the model to think harder” with no new tokens of evidence.
05Config path

There is no Control Hub page for the forward pass. The admin surfaces are the provider console (key, project, model entitlement, usage) and the request body your service sends. The contact-center admin path still matters: the route that sends a caller to this bot lives in Webex Control Hub, UCCE scripting, or CUCM dial-plan and trunk config. Check the admin guide for the product version that owns the route. Click paths differ by product and release. This list is the model side, which you can rehearse without a tenant.

items: Create a project and a key in the provider console. Do not paste the key into a room, a prompt, or a trace. Screenshot the project name only.
Confirm the model id you intend to call is on the project’s allow list. The reference may list ids your key cannot use. Record the id string you will pin.

Choose one sampling knob. For a factual summary, start from the guide’s “more focused” side of temperature (their example of a lower value is 0.2) and leave top_p untouched, matching the “not both” guidance. [cite:4]
Put abstention and format rules in `instructions` when you use the Responses API, because that channel is documented to take priority over `input`. [cite:3]

Set a max output bound so a runaway sample cannot burn the call’s latency budget. On Chat Completions the reference names `max_completion_tokens` as an upper bound that includes visible output tokens and reasoning tokens, and it marks `max_tokens` deprecated in favor of that field and incompatible with o-series models. The token-counting guide names `max_output_tokens` as the Responses API counterpart, and it says both limits count tokens the model generates, including tokens that are not visible. [cite:4] [cite:8]
Request logprobs only when you have a consumer for them. On chat completions, `top_logprobs` without `logprobs: true` is invalid. [cite:4]
Log model id, token usage, finish reason, and the prompt version. Do not log the raw key. Do not log customer speech until T8 says the retention rule.
Read the text through the SDK’s aggregated text helper, or walk the output array. Do not index `output[0]` and hope. [cite:3]

blocks.text: Dependencies you actually need for the lab in this room: a pencil for the softmax, and optionally a provider account. You do not need a vector database, an MCP server, or a GPU. As of 2026-10-14 the LlamaIndex framework docs state that the framework is MIT-licensed, and the pgvector LICENSE file on master is the PostgreSQL-style grant (portions copyright PostgreSQL Global Development Group and the UC Regents). Read the LICENSE in any other SDK commit you install. [cite:18] [cite:19] This page links docs; it does not redistribute them.
07Troubleshooting
Eight failures you will meet. The fix column is a check you can perform, not a superstition.

rows: Same prompt, different wording every call
Sampling. The distribution has mass on more than one token.
Temperature, top_p, and whether both are set. Optional logprobs on the first generated token.

Lower one knob, not both. If you need repeatable text, Chat Completions documents a beta `seed`: the same seed and the same parameters are a best effort, determinism is not guaranteed, and you watch `system_fingerprint` for backend changes. That is not a proof that temperature 0 is greedy. [cite:4]
The model ignores a paragraph in the middle of a long prompt

The tokens never entered the window, or they entered and the instruction did not force their use. Liu et al. (arXiv:2307.03172, historical) report a U-shaped curve: their models used information at the beginning or end of a long context better than information in the middle. One figure they report is GPT-3.5-Turbo on their multi-document QA task falling below its closed-book score of 56.1% when the relevant document sat in the middle. That number is their experiment, not a 2026 product score. [cite:12]
Token count of the request versus the model’s window. The exact rendered prompt, not the fragments you think you sent.
Count tokens with the provider’s method. Cut or move the paragraph. If the fact is a document, stop pasting and move to T3.
You read the wrong field. Responses can carry non-text items first.
The raw output array and the finish reason.
Use the documented text aggregator or walk items by type. [cite:3]
Output feels both “creative” and unstable after a tuning pass
Temperature and top_p were changed together.
The request body in the trace.
Reset one parameter to the API default and sweep the other. [cite:4]
The flag was off, the field was requested on an endpoint that uses a different name, or top_logprobs was sent alone.
The request JSON and the response schema.
On chat completions, set logprobs true before top_logprobs. [cite:4] This room does not name the field on other APIs.
Request rejected for length while the paragraph “looks short”
Tokens are not words. A table, a code block, or a non-Latin script can be many ids per word.
A tokenizer count from the same provider as the model. A count from a different tokenizer is the wrong ruler.
Count with the matching tokenizer. The embedding API’s 8192 cap is not the chat cap. [cite:6]
Nearest-neighbor search over “the model’s embeddings” returns nonsense
You stored vectors from one model and queried with another, or you stored hidden states you were not supposed to compare, or you used a distance the index was not built for.
The model id written beside each vector. The distance function. OpenAI recommends cosine for their embedding guide. [cite:5]
Re-embed query and corpus with one model id. Details of index rebuild are T3.
A voice bot speaks a sentence that stops mid-word
The text was cut by a max-token cap, or TTS started before the model finished, or barge-in cut playback.
Finish reason (length versus stop). Whether the client streamed audio from a partial transcript.
If finish reason is length, raise the cap or shorten the instruction. If the text is complete and the audio is not, the bug is in T7’s voice stack, not in attention.
A benign contact-center utterance is refused
A safety policy on the provider side, or your own instruction over-triggered.
The refusal string versus your instruction. Whether the utterance contains words you banned.

Read the instruction first. The Llama 4 card points at an Acceptable Use Policy rather than pasting the policy into the architecture section. [cite:23] OpenAI’s safety-policy text was not fetched for this sentence. Do not “jailbreak” a policy in this lab.
Overnight cost spike with flat traffic
A retry loop, a longer prompt (retrieved junk, or a growing history), or a silent model-id change onto a pricier SKU.
Usage tokens per request, model id, retry count.
Pin the model id. Cap history. Price math uses the pricing page fetched 2026-10-14. [cite:9]

blocks.text: 08Self-question ladder
Open a node, answer out loud, then open the child. A leaf ends in a citation or a TODO-verify. Stop when you can say the leaf without looking.
L0 · What is a language model, in one sentence?
A language model assigns a probability to the next token given the tokens so far, and a sampler turns that distribution into the token you append. [cite:1]
L1 · Why does next-token prediction exist, and what breaks if you treat the model as a database?

The Transformer was built as a sequence transducer: it predicts from context it can attend to, it does not commit to storing a retrievable record with a primary key. If you treat it as a database, updates do not land until you retrain or you put the new fact in the window, and you get no provenance. The RAG paper states both problems directly: manipulating knowledge precisely is limited, and provenance plus updating world knowledge were open problems for parametric models. [cite:7]
L2 · How does a string become the next token, end to end?

The API renders messages into a string, the tokenizer emits ids, embeddings plus a positional signal enter the stack, each block mixes positions with masked attention and a feed-forward sub-layer, the last projection emits logits, softmax (after temperature or nucleus) yields a distribution, one id is chosen, and the loop repeats until stop. Then ids become text. [cite:1] [cite:3]
L2 · Where does word order enter if attention itself has no recurrence?

The paper adds positional encodings to the embeddings because the model has no recurrence and no convolution. Sinusoidal encodings and learned positional embeddings scored nearly the same in their experiment. [cite:1] Meta’s Llama 4 blog, fetched 2026-10-14, names iRoPE for that family: RoPE on most layers, interleaved layers without positional embeddings, and inference-time temperature scaling of attention. The OpenAI models page fetched the same day does not name a scheme. [cite:21] [cite:10]
L3 · The answer is wrong. How do I prove whether the failure is sampling, attention, or missing knowledge?

Collect the rendered prompt, the model id, temperature, top_p, finish reason, and — if you asked — logprobs. If the needed fact is not in the prompt and not something you can defend from the system card’s training description, call it missing knowledge and go to retrieval or a tool. If the fact is in the prompt and logprobs show a close second token, call it sampling and sweep one knob. If the fact is in the prompt, the probability of the bad continuation is high, and a shorter prompt that contains only that fact answers correctly, suspect distraction or instruction priority, not “broken attention,” and test by moving the fact and tightening the instruction. A picture of one attention head is not proof. [cite:4]
L3 · What single change separates a sampling bug from a retrieval bug?

Put the gold sentence alone in the context and set a focused temperature, leaving top_p at default. If the model now states the sentence, the weights and the sampler can express it, and the earlier failure was the absence or the burial of evidence. If it still invents a different fact, you are looking at instruction-following or a refusal, not at a missing index. [cite:4] [cite:7]
L4 · How does this differ across OpenAI, Anthropic, and an open-weight runtime?

The computation — ids, a frozen network, a sampler — is the shared idea. The contract differs. OpenAI’s text guide tells you to prefer the Responses API and to treat `instructions` as higher priority than `input`. [cite:3] Anthropic’s message and tool schema is taught in T4, not copied here. An open-weight runtime makes the sampler and the chat template your problem. The Llama 4 Community License is the file beside those weights, fetched 2026-10-14. [cite:22] The chat template and the tokenizer merge table live in the generation cookbook, which this pass did not read, This room does not name that template. Do not claim feature parity.
L4 · How does the same model sit on a Webex or UCCE call?

The phone system still owns the leg: SIP or the CCaaS task, the queue, the recording decision. Speech recognition produces the text that becomes the user message. The model computes the next tokens of a reply or a tool request. Speech synthesis speaks the text. Transfer back to a human is a routing action, not a token. Check the admin guide for the product version on the tenant. Variable names differ by product and release. The computation in this room does not change when the caller is on CUCM.
L5 · If I redesigned the decoder, what would I change, and what stops me?

I would want a longer reliable use of evidence in the middle of the window, a cheaper way to reuse previous keys and values, and a sampler default that does not surprise an on-call engineer. The constraint is not a slogan about scale. It is whatever the serving stack and the model card actually guarantee: memory for the cache, the trained positional scheme, and the latency budget of a phone call. Check the serving stack for cache bytes; they vary with length, layers, precision, and batch. Check your hop traces for a phone-call millisecond budget; it varies with the edge. The 2017 paper already records the motive for positions that might extrapolate past the trained length, and it also records that learned positions merely matched sinusoids in their test — extrapolation was a hypothesis, not a measured promise for today’s windows. [cite:1]
L5 · What would an infinite context window still not give me?

Provenance, an update path that does not require rereading the entire corpus into the prompt, and a price I can pay per call. The RAG paper’s reason for a non-parametric index is that you can replace that memory when the world changes. [cite:7] A huge window is still parametric-plus-paste. It does not by itself cite a paragraph or drop a stale one.
Leaf · What does temperature multiply or divide?

In the definition used in this room, temperature divides the logits before softmax. It does not scale attention weights inside the block. The worked numbers are in the deep dive. The vendor still owns the exact implementation, including temperature 0. [cite:4] The page does not say that 0 is greedy argmax, and this room does not claim that it is.
Leaf · Why is cosine the default for retrieval embeddings but not the score inside attention?

They are different objects. Attention uses scaled dot products of learned queries and keys, then softmax, as written in the Transformer paper. [cite:1] Retrieval embeddings are compared across documents; OpenAI’s embedding guide recommends cosine similarity for that search. [cite:5] Cosine is not “how attention works.”
Leaf · What would I measure before I fine-tune?

Whether the failure survives a focused temperature and a prompt that already contains the gold fact. If it does not survive, fine-tuning is the wrong tool. The comparison protocol is T6-R01 and T6-R06. The principle follows from the three places a fact can live, plus the sampler docs. [cite:4]
09Lab
No API key is required. The point is to compute the objects the room names. Optional steps that need a key are marked and can be skipped.

items: Goal: by hand, turn three logits into probabilities at two temperatures, apply a nucleus cutoff, and write five sentences that use only those results.

Prerequisites: this room’s deep dive. A provider account is optional. No tenant, no Control Hub, no GPU. LlamaIndex’s framework docs say MIT, and pgvector’s LICENSE on master is the PostgreSQL-style grant, both read 2026-10-14. [cite:18] [cite:19]
Step 1. Logits 2, 1, 0. Compute softmax at T = 1 using the shifted-logit method. Expected: probabilities about 0.665, 0.245, 0.090.
Step 2. Divide logits by 0.5 and by 2. Recompute. Expected: the top token’s mass rises at 0.5 (about 0.867) and falls at 2 (about 0.507).
Step 3. On the T = 1 distribution, apply nucleus p = 0.9 and p = 0.5. Expected: two tokens survive at 0.9; one survives at 0.5. Renormalize and write the new probabilities.
Step 4. Query [1, 0], keys [1, 0] and [0, 1], d_k = 2. Compute scaled scores and softmax weights. Expected: about 0.670 and 0.330.
Step 5. In one paragraph, state which of those operations lives in the sampler and which lives in the block. Expected: temperature and nucleus in the sampler; scaled dots in the block.
Evidence: a photo or a notebook page with the four calculations and the paragraph. Keep it in your private notes, not in this repo if it later includes a key.

Break-it: set temperature to 0.2 and top_p to 0.1 at the same time on paper, and write why you could not attribute a behavior change to either knob. Recovery: restore top_p to “untouched” and keep a single knob, matching the chat-completions guidance. [cite:4]

Optional, only if you already have a key: send one short completion with logprobs enabled on an endpoint that documents them, and confirm the response carries a logprob per output token. Do not invent the call if the field name differs. This room does not name a logprobs field on Responses. [cite:4]
Reflection: what surprised you — the size of the tail at T = 1, or the fact that attention still leaked a third of the unmatched value?

blocks.text: 10Quiz
Multiple choice
Q1. What does one forward pass of the language model directly produce?

items: A finished paragraph.
A vector of scores over the vocabulary for the next token.
A row from a database.
An embedding you should insert into a vector index.

blocks.text: Reveal
B. The paragraph is a loop of samples, detokenized. The retrieval embedding is a different model. [cite:1]
Multiple choice
Q2. Why does the Transformer paper divide the query–key dot products by the square root of d_k?

items: To convert the score into a probability by itself.
Because unscaled dots grow in magnitude with d_k and push softmax into a region of tiny gradients.
To implement nucleus sampling.
To add word order.

blocks.text: Reveal
B. Softmax, not the scale, makes the weights. Positions are added separately. Nucleus sampling is not in that paper. [cite:1]
Multiple choice
Q3. OpenAI’s chat-completions reference tells you to treat temperature and top_p how?

items: Always set both, or the call is rejected.
Alter one or the other, not both.
top_p replaces the network.
Temperature is an integer count of tokens.

blocks.text: Reveal
B. Temperature is documented from 0 to 2. top_p is nucleus mass. [cite:4]
Multiple choice
Q4. Nucleus sampling with threshold p keeps which set?

items: A fixed top-k chosen yesterday.
The smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p.
Every token with logit greater than p.
Only the single mode.

blocks.text: Reveal
B. That is Holtzman’s definition, and the set changes size step to step. [cite:2]
Multiple choice
Q5. Default widths in OpenAI’s embedding guide for text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large are:

items: 512 and 768, the Transformer paper’s widths.
Whatever the chat model’s hidden size is.

blocks.text: Reveal
B. 8192 is the documented per-input token cap on the embeddings API, not the vector width. [cite:5] [cite:6]
Scenario
Q6. A bot answers a billing question with a confident, specific, and false credit. The policy PDF was never retrieved. What is the first change?

items: Raise temperature so it explores a correction.
Fine-tune on yesterday’s calls.
Put the policy text in context or behind a tool, and add an abstention rule when it is absent.
Increase d_k.

blocks.text: Reveal
C. The fact is in neither the weights you can update today nor the context. Temperature will not fetch a PDF. Fine-tuning is a later decision, after a prompt-and-retrieve baseline exists. [cite:7]
Scenario
Q7. Your client prints an empty string from a Responses call that the playground shows as a normal sentence. What do you inspect?

items: Assume the model returned no tokens.
The output array’s item types, and any SDK helper that aggregates text. The guide says not to assume text is at output index zero.
The BLEU score of the 2017 paper.
The vector index.

blocks.text: Reveal
B. [cite:3]
Scenario
Q8. Logprobs show the chosen token at logprob −0.05 and the runner-up at −3.1, and the chosen token contradicts a sentence that is present in the prompt. Which bucket is the weak fit?

items: “The sampler was torn between two phrasings.”
“The model was unsure.”
“A sampling coin-flip.” The mass is peaked. Look at instruction priority and whether the sentence was actually in the rendered prompt.
“The tokenizer is down.”

blocks.text: Reveal
C. A logprob near zero means probability near one. Close alternatives would have logprobs near the winner. Presence in the rendered prompt is the check. [cite:4]
Draw it
Q9. On paper, draw seven boxes from text back to text and mark where temperature sits.
Reveal
Text, token ids, embed plus position, blocks, logits, sample, text. Temperature sits in the sample box, between logits and the chosen id. Attention sits in the blocks. [cite:1] [cite:4]
Draw it
Q10. Draw the causal mask for three positions. Which scores are legal?
Reveal

Position 1 sees only itself. Position 2 sees 1 and 2. Position 3 sees 1, 2, and 3. Future scores are set so softmax gives them no weight. The paper describes masking illegal connections before the softmax. [cite:1]
Short answer
Q11. Name the documented priority between OpenAI `instructions` and `input` on the text-generation guide.
Reveal
Instructions provided that way take priority over a prompt in `input`. [cite:3]
Short answer
Q12. A teammate quotes 28.4 BLEU as “how good Transformers are now.” What do you say?
Reveal
28.4 is the big Transformer’s WMT 2014 English-to-German score in the 2017 paper, a historical result, not a 2026 leaderboard. The architecture lessons survive; the number does not travel. [cite:1]
Short answer
Q13. What does Chat Completions promise if you send the same `seed` twice?
Reveal

A best effort at the same result when the other parameters match. The reference calls the feature beta, says determinism is not guaranteed, and points you at `system_fingerprint` to notice backend changes. It does not say temperature 0 is greedy. [cite:4]
Short answer
Q14. Name the output-cap field on Chat Completions and the one the token-counting guide names for the Responses API.
Reveal

`max_completion_tokens` on Chat Completions, which includes visible output and reasoning tokens. `max_tokens` is documented as deprecated in favor of it and incompatible with o-series models. The token-counting guide names `max_output_tokens` for Responses, and says both caps count generated tokens, including tokens you do not see. [cite:4] [cite:8]

blocks.text: Integration map

Application renders messages → provider API → tokenizer and network and sampler → text and usage → application log. A vector store is not on this path until T3. An MCP server is not on this path until T4. A phone system is upstream of the application: it delivers audio, not logits.
Cross-platform bridges

items: OpenAI Responses versus chat completions: same scores-and-sample idea, different JSON. The text guide tells new work to prefer Responses. [cite:3]
OpenAI versus Anthropic versus an open-weight server: bridge the task and the abstention rule, not the field names. Anthropic details are T4. This room does not name an open-weight chat template.

CUCM, Webex Contact Center, UCCE → this model: bridge a transcript and a task id in; bridge a reply and a transfer decision out. Do not bridge SIP headers into the prompt unless a documented tool needs them. This room does not reproduce admin menus.

title: Transformers and attention, walked through
summary: Attention is a weighted sum of value vectors. The weights come from scaled dots between a query and the keys. This room walks that formula with numbers, then says what a 2026 model card adds and what it still refuses to draw.

blocks.title: Verification
blocks.text: Source note: last-verified was left unmarked until a person checks the cited pages. The citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date.

Attention is a weighted sum of value vectors. The weights come from scaled dots between a query and the keys. This room walks that formula with numbers, then says what a 2026 model card adds and what it still refuses to draw.
01Executive summary

items: Vaswani et al. define scaled dot-product attention as softmax of QK transpose, divided by the square root of the key dimension, times V. Multi-head attention runs that several times and concatenates. The base model in the paper is 6 layers, d_model 512, 8 heads, d_k 64, and a feed-forward inner width of 2048. Those integers are the 2017 experiment, not a product you can call. [cite:1]

The decoder uses a causal mask so a position cannot attend to future tokens. The paper also has encoder–decoder attention. A chat model often keeps only the causal decoder stack. Confirm that on the card. The Llama 4 card says auto-regressive mixture-of-experts with early fusion. It does not publish a Vaswani layer diagram. [cite:1] [cite:2]

Residuals and layer normalization sit around each sublayer in the paper: the sublayer output is added back to its input, then normalized. The feed-forward sublayer is position-wise. It is not the retrieval index. [cite:1]

Meta’s Llama 4 blog names iRoPE: RoPE on most layers, interleaved layers with no positional embeddings, and inference-time temperature scaling of attention. Scout’s card lists a 10 million-token context. The blog says Scout was pre-trained and post-trained with a 256K context length, “which empowers the base model with advanced length generalization capability,” and it separately names a supported context of 10 million tokens. Keep both. [cite:3] [cite:2]

Temperature in the sampler divides logits before the next-token softmax. It is a different knob from the attention-temperature scaling the Llama 4 blog describes inside the block. Do not collapse them. [cite:4] [cite:3]

blocks.title: Why it matters for the lab engineer
blocks.text: A contact-center demo that “shows attention” is often a heatmap with no claim you can defend. This room is the defense: you can compute one head by hand, you can say what the mask removes, and you can refuse to treat a product screenshot as the 2017 diagram or as a faithful explanation of a sentence. The caller still hears text. The math is how you stop inventing a reason the bot said the wrong credit.
02Architecture
One query, two keys, a scale, a softmax, and a mix of values. Teaching numbers, not a vendor diagram.
Where attention sits in a decoder block, between the residual stream and the feed-forward sublayer.
Diagram: Seven stages from token embeddings through masked attention, residual, feed-forward, and logits

items: 1–2 are embeddings plus a positional scheme. The 2017 paper adds sinusoids because there is no recurrence.
3 is masked self-attention. Future positions are not keys for this token.
4–6 are the residual, the position-wise feed-forward, and the next residual. 7 is the logit vector T1 already taught.

blocks.text: Sequence: one new token reuses cached keys and values from earlier positions.
Diagram: App, embedder, attention block, feed-forward, sampler, and the cache of past keys and values

The sequence picture is the decode loop. The first token of a reply attends over the prompt. Each later token attends over the prompt and the tokens already chosen, under the causal mask. A cache stores keys and values so the server does not recompute them. Check the serving stack you run for cache memory. The byte size varies with sequence length, layer count, precision, and batch, which is why a model card does not carry one number.
03Deep dive

Start from the sentence the paper actually writes. Attention maps a query and a set of key–value pairs to an output. The output is a weighted sum of the values. The weight on a value is the compatibility of the query with that value’s key. Scaled dot-product attention computes the compatibility as a dot product, divides by the square root of the key dimension, and applies softmax. The division is there so the dots do not grow with dimension and push softmax into a region with tiny gradients. That is a training motive in the paper. It is also the reason a hand calculation at d_k = 2 looks milder than the raw dots. [cite:1]
One query, two keys, arithmetic you can recompute

Let the query be [1, 0]. Let the keys be [1, 0] and [0, 1]. The key dimension d_k is 2, so the scale is the square root of 2, about 1.414. The raw dots are 1 and 0. The scaled scores are about 0.707 and 0. Softmax of those two numbers is about 0.670 and 0.330. The first key wins, and it does not take all the mass. If the values are [1, 0] and [0, 1], the mixed output is about [0.670, 0.330]. Nothing in that paragraph is a vendor guarantee. It is the formula on two vectors you can write on paper. The same pair is the toy on the T1 flashcard. If your calculator disagrees at the second decimal, recompute the exponentials before you “fix” the architecture.

rows: Not cosine. Cosine would divide by the norms. OpenAI recommends cosine for embeddings, which is a different comparison. [cite:5]
Not temperature. Sampler temperature divides logits later. [cite:4]
Not a citation and not an explanation of a sentence.
Not the token the sampler will pick. That choice is a later softmax over the vocabulary.

blocks.title: Attention weights are not the reason
blocks.text: A product that paints these weights on the words and calls the brightest word “why the model said it” is making a claim this room does not grant. The paper defines a mixing operation. It does not define a faithful explanation. Check that product’s own evaluation before you call a map the reason. Whether the brightest token explains the output varies by model and by task.
The mask

In the decoder, self-attention is masked so that position i does not attend to positions after i. The paper implements that by setting those future scores to negative infinity before softmax, which drives the corresponding weights to zero. The model can still attend to earlier tokens, including the prompt. It cannot peek at the token it has not produced yet. That is the causal constraint. Encoder self-attention in the same paper is not masked that way: every position in the encoder may attend to every other position in the input sequence. Chat products that only generate left to right are using the causal idea. They are not required to ship the encoder. [cite:1]

Apply the mask to the toy before you celebrate the 0.67. If the second key is a future token, its score becomes negative infinity, its weight becomes zero, and the output collapses to the first value. A demo that forgets the mask will show the model “looking ahead” in a picture that the decoder is not allowed to compute. When you debug a wrong answer, the mask is not the first place to look. The prompt, the tool result, and the sampler are. The mask is the place to look when someone claims the model read a token that had not been generated.
Multi-head, residuals, and the feed-forward sublayer

One head is one set of projections. Multi-head attention runs h heads, each with its own learned projections of the same input into queries, keys, and values, computes attention in each head, concatenates, and applies a final projection. The paper sets d_k = d_v = d_model / h. In the base model, d_model is 512 and h is 8, so each head has d_k 64. The big model in the paper is larger. Quote the row you mean. Do not say “transformers have 8 heads” as if that were a 2026 constant. [cite:1]

headers: Base model in Vaswani et al.
rows: Historical. Llama 4’s card does not publish a layer count of this kind. [cite:2]
The residual width in that experiment. Not an embedding-API width. text-embedding-3-small defaults to 1536. [cite:5]
Historical. Do not copy onto Scout or onto gpt-6-astra.
Inner width of the position-wise feed-forward network in the base model.
A 2014 translation score reported in 2017. Not contact-center quality.

blocks.text: Around each sublayer the paper uses a residual connection and layer normalization. The input to the next sublayer is the normalized sum of the sublayer input and the sublayer output. The residual is why people say the block “adds” attention to the stream instead of replacing the stream. If you remove the residual in a lecture sketch, you have drawn a different network. The feed-forward sublayer is applied to each position separately and identically. It is two linear maps with a ReLU between them in the paper. It mixes features at one position. It does not mix positions. Attention mixed the positions. The feed-forward network does not retrieve a PDF. Retrieval is T3.

blocks.title: Three mixes, three jobs
blocks.text: Attention mixes across positions. The feed-forward sublayer mixes across features at one position. The sampler mixes nothing: it picks an id from a distribution over the vocabulary. When a teammate says “the attention hallucinated,” ask which of the three they mean. Usually they mean the sampler emitted a token the pack did not support. That bug is faithfulness, taught in T3 and T5, not a broken scale factor.
What Llama 4 actually changes in the story

The Llama 4 model card, fetched 2026-10-14, describes Scout and Maverick as auto-regressive language models that are mixture-of-experts, early fusion, and natively multimodal. Scout activates 17 billion parameters out of 109 billion total, with 16 experts. Maverick activates 17 billion out of 400 billion, with 128 experts. Supported languages on the card are Arabic, English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Tagalog, Thai, and Vietnamese. Image understanding was tested up to five input images. Instruction-tuned checkpoints are for assistant-like chat and visual reasoning. Pretrained checkpoints can be adapted for natural-language generation. The card does not name RLHF or DPO. [cite:2]

The blog, fetched the same day, names iRoPE. Most layers use rotary position embeddings. Some layers are interleaved with no positional embeddings. Attention temperature is scaled at inference time. Scout was pre-trained and post-trained at a 256 thousand-token context. The blog attaches “advanced length generalization capability” to that sentence. The card’s context-length field for Scout is 10 million, which the blog also names as the supported context, and the blog reports results over 10 million tokens of code. Maverick’s card lists 1 million. Knowledge cutoff on both cards is August 2024. Training compute on the card: Scout 5.0 million GPU hours, Maverick 2.38 million, 7.38 million total, on H100 80 GB accelerators at 700 W TDP. Location-based greenhouse gas is 1,999 tons CO2eq. Market-based is 0 because the card says Meta has run net-zero operations since 2020. Those figures are the card’s. They are not a serving latency and not a contact-center SLA. [cite:3] [cite:2]

rows: Model card. Blog adds the 256K train length for Scout. [cite:3]
iRoPE, as the blog describes it. Not printed as a layer diagram on the card.

blocks.text: OpenAI’s models page, fetched 2026-10-14, lists gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, and gpt-6-luna at a 1.05 million-token context and a 128 thousand-token max output. It does not publish depth, width, head count, or a positional scheme. You can compare context windows. You cannot compare head counts, because one side did not publish them. Behemoth appears in the blog as a previewed teacher, not as a model-card file this room read as a shipped checkpoint. Do not quiz a teammate on Behemoth’s layer count. [cite:6] [cite:3]
Where this sits next to retrieval and tools

Attention inside the block reads the tokens that are already in the window. It does not open a database. If the refund policy is not in the prompt, no head will retrieve it. Packing a chunk into the window, which T3 teaches, gives attention something to mix. A tool result, which T4 teaches, is more tokens in that same window after the host executes. The host does not run inside a head. MCP revision 2025-11-25 keeps execution in the host. The changelog’s sampling-with-tools change asks the client to sample. It does not move the side effect into Q, K, or V. [cite:7]

Lost-in-the-middle, Liu et al., is a historical claim that models can use information at the start and end of a long context better than information in the middle. The paper is arXiv:2307.03172. It is not a measurement of Scout’s 10 million-token window and not a measurement of your contact-center prompt. Cite it as a reason to test position, not as a score you can paste onto a bot. [cite:8]
Four prompts, the same head

Keep the toy head fixed and change only the tokens you imagine in the window. The arithmetic does not become a vendor trace. It becomes a way to talk about four contact-center failures without blaming “attention” for all of them.

Prompt A is the policy paragraph at the start and the caller’s sentence at the end: “credits over fifty dollars need a human.” The query at the last position can put weight on “fifty” and on “human.” If the sample then says “I have applied a two hundred dollar credit,” the failure is not that the dot product was undefined. The failure is that a token was chosen which the policy paragraph does not authorize, and that a tool, if one ran, was allowed to commit. Attention could have mixed the word “fifty” into the last position and the sampler could still have picked “two hundred.” Mixing is not obedience. The fix is the tool cap from T4 and the faithfulness check from T5, not a larger d_k.

Prompt B moves the same policy sentence into the middle of a long transcript, with small talk on both sides. Liu et al. would tell you to suspect the middle. Your job is smaller: copy the sentence to the end, call the model again on a fixture, and see whether the abstention returns. If it returns, you have a position effect on this id, and you still do not have their tables. If it does not return, the model was not using the sentence even when it was adjacent to the query, and rearranging the prompt will not save you. Write down which of those two you observed. A story about “lost in the middle” without that swap is a citation wearing a costume. [cite:8]

Prompt C is a tool result that arrived after the caller barged in. The text in the window says the assistant already finished a sentence the caller never heard, because nobody truncated. Attention will mix that unheard sentence into the next query, because the mask only hides the future, not the past you failed to delete. The repair is T7’s truncate, not a new positional scheme. iRoPE does not know which audio reached the speaker. The blog’s temperature scaling of attention will not drop tokens you left in the prefix. [cite:3]

Prompt D is an empty window except the user text “what is the outage in Dallas?” No status page was packed. Every head, at every width the paper ever used, can only mix the words Dallas and outage with whatever the weights already store. The next token may be fluent. It is not a reading of a page you did not provide. This is the same boundary T1-R01 draws among weights, the window, and a tool. Attention is the mixer of the window. It is not a fourth place a fact can live.

Across the four prompts the head’s formula did not change. The mask did not change. What changed was the set of keys. When you are on call, ask “which keys were in the prefix?” before you ask “is attention broken?” The prefix is the prompt you built, the tool results the host appended, and the tokens the sampler already chose. The projections are the vendor’s, unless you are serving a checkpoint whose license you have read. For Llama 4 that license is the Community License. For an API model the projections are not yours to edit, and the card may not even list their shapes. [cite:9] [cite:6]

A useful review habit is to separate three sentences you are otherwise tempted to fuse. Sentence one: “the 2017 block has residual attention and a position-wise feed-forward network.” Sentence two: “Llama 4 Scout is a mixture-of-experts model with 16 experts and a 10 million context field on the card.” Sentence three: “this bot’s last answer contradicted paragraph 4.” Only sentence three is an incident. Sentence one explains a paper. Sentence two explains a card. Neither sentence selects a root cause for the credit. People who skip to a heatmap are trying to make sentence one do sentence three’s job. It cannot.

If you teach this room out loud, compute the toy once on a board and then refuse every follow-up that asks for Scout’s head count. The refusal is the lesson. The card spent its numbers on experts, active parameters, context, tokens, cutoff, GPU hours, and emissions. It did not spend them on h or d_model. An interviewer who wants eight heads wants the paper. Give them the paper, labeled historical, and then give them the card. Candidates who can only give one of those two will ship a diagram that matches neither system. [cite:1] [cite:2]

One more distinction belongs in the same breath as the experts. A mixture-of-experts model does not run every expert on every token. The card’s “17 billion activated” against “109 billion total” is the sentence that says so for Scout, and the same shape, with 128 experts and 400 billion total, is Maverick. The routing that picks experts is not drawn in the card and not drawn in this room. Do not invent a router diagram and attribute it to Meta. What you can say is that the active count is the compute the card claims per token, and the total count is the parameters that exist. Interviewers who add 17 and 109 have misread both numbers. Active is not a remainder. [cite:2]

Early fusion, the other phrase on that card, means the model is natively multimodal rather than a text model with a vision encoder bolted on in a way the card would have had to describe separately. The card says input can be multilingual text and image, and output is multilingual text and code. It says image understanding was tested with up to five images. It does not say a contact-center screenshot is in domain, and it does not publish a word-error rate for a phone call. Bring images into a lab only when the card’s input column includes them, and still evaluate the task you care about. A five-image test on the card is not a five-screenshot warranty for a desktop assist product. [cite:2]

Supported languages on the card are twelve: Arabic, English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Tagalog, Thai, and Vietnamese. The card also points at a broader pretraining mixture and at the No Language Left Behind work for a set on the order of two hundred languages. Those are different claims. A bot that must answer in a language outside the twelve should not be justified by the two-hundred figure alone. Say which list you are using. The same care applies to the emissions line: 1,999 tons CO2eq location-based, and zero market-based because the card states net-zero operations since 2020. Neither number is a latency budget. Both are part of reading a card all the way down, which is the habit this track is for. [cite:2]
04Walk-through

A caller says “you charged me twice.” The application has already decided, outside the model, that the allowed context is the last four turns plus one policy paragraph. This walk-through is the forward pass on that string. It is not the dial plan.

items: Tokenize. The rendered prompt, including whatever template the provider owns, becomes integer ids. The lab’s tokenizer is a toy. Check the tokenizer docs for the model id you call. Merge rules differ by family, which is why the toy table is not the production one.

Embed and position. Each id becomes a vector. The 2017 paper adds a positional encoding because the network has no recurrence and no convolution. A Llama 4 checkpoint, per the blog, uses iRoPE instead of that sinusoid. An OpenAI chat id on the fetched models page does not name its scheme. [cite:1] [cite:3]

Masked attention. For the newest position, queries dot with keys of this position and earlier positions only. Scale, softmax, mix values. Several heads, then the output projection. The toy numbers above are the shape of this step at d_k = 2, not the shape inside Scout.

Residual and feed-forward. Add the attention output back, normalize as the paper’s block does, run the position-wise network, add and normalize again. Repeat for the stack depth the card actually states. If the card is silent, say silent.

Logits and sample. The last position’s vector becomes a score per vocabulary id. Temperature, if you set it, divides those logits. OpenAI’s chat-completions reference documents a temperature between 0 and 2 and says it generally recommends altering temperature or top_p, but not both. That page does not say that 0 is greedy argmax. Check the sampling section of the endpoint you call. Behavior at the bottom of the range varies by implementation, which is why this room will not teach that 0 means argmax. [cite:4]

Append and repeat. The chosen id is appended. Its key and value can be cached. The next position attends over a longer prefix. Stop on a finish condition or a length cap. max_completion_tokens on that OpenAI reference includes reasoning tokens. [cite:4]

blocks.text: If step 3 is pictured as a heatmap on the words “charged” and “twice,” you still have not shown that the refund tool should run. The heatmap is a mixing weight. The tool decision is a later sample, and the host still has to allow it. T4 is the allow. This room is the mix.
05Config path

There is no switch labeled “attention” in a normal chat request. You configure the model id, the prompt, and the sampler. The projections were learned before you called. The path below is what you can rehearse without a provider console. Check the console for the account you use. Menu labels differ by product and by tenant, which is why a screenshot from another org is not a step.

items: Read the model card for the id you will call. For Llama 4, that card is the Scout and Maverick file cited here. For the OpenAI ids in T1-R01, use the models page and accept that depth and width are absent. [cite:2] [cite:6]
Record context length and max output from that page, with the fetch date. Do not copy 512 or 8 heads into the record.
If you serve the weights, read the license beside them. Llama 4 is the Community License, effective 5 April 2025, not MIT. [cite:9]
Set sampler fields from the API reference you actually call. The chat-completions reference recommends altering temperature or top_p, but not both. It does not forbid sending both. [cite:4]
Leave attention-temperature scaling alone unless the runtime documents it. The Llama 4 blog describes it as part of iRoPE inference. It is not the request body’s temperature field. [cite:3]
Refuse any debug UI that claims a faithful explanation until that claim has a source. The mark on that claim stays until the source exists.

Grade the answer against the pack. Leave the product claim marked.

The fetched OpenAI page does not say mixture-of-experts. [cite:6]

A position effect you have not measured

blocks.text: 08Self-question ladder
Answer out loud. A leaf ends in a citation or a TODO-verify.
L0 · What does one attention head output?
A vector that is a weighted sum of value vectors. The weights are a softmax of scaled query–key dots. [cite:1]
L1 · Why divide by the square root of d_k?
The paper’s reason is to keep the dots from growing with dimension and saturating softmax. In the toy, d_k is 2, so you divide by about 1.414 before the exponentials. [cite:1]
L1 · What does the causal mask change in the toy?
If the second key is in the future, its score is negative infinity and its weight is zero. The output is the first value alone. [cite:1]
L2 · What is multi-head attention in the paper?
h independent attention computations, concatenated, then projected. The base model uses h = 8 and d_model = 512, so d_k = 64. Historical. [cite:1]
L2 · What does the residual do?
It adds the sublayer output back to the sublayer input before layer normalization, so the block updates the stream instead of replacing it. [cite:1]
L2 · What does the feed-forward sublayer mix?
Features at a single position. It does not mix across positions. Attention already did that. The base inner width is 2048. [cite:1]
L3 · Is a chat model the 2017 encoder–decoder?

Not by default. The paper has both stacks and three uses of attention. A chat model is often decoder-only. Llama 4’s card says auto-regressive mixture-of-experts and does not draw the 2017 diagram. [cite:2]
L3 · What is iRoPE, and where did you read it?

The Llama 4 blog: RoPE on most layers, interleaved layers without positional embeddings, and inference-time temperature scaling of attention. The model card’s context field is a different sentence from the blog’s 256K training length. [cite:3]
L3 · Scout versus Maverick, in one breath?

Both activate 17 billion parameters. Scout is 109 billion total, 16 experts, 10 million context on the card, about 40 trillion tokens. Maverick is 400 billion total, 128 experts, 1 million context, about 22 trillion tokens. Cutoff August 2024. [cite:2]
L4 · Why is sampler temperature not attention temperature?
OpenAI’s chat reference divides logits by temperature before the vocabulary softmax, range 0 to 2. The blog’s attention-temperature scaling is inside iRoPE. Different objects. [cite:4] [cite:3]
L4 · What must you not copy from the paper onto gpt-6-astra?
Layer count, head count, and d_model. The models page fetched 2026-10-14 publishes context and max output, not those widths. [cite:6]
L5 · If you redesigned the debug UI, what would you change, and what stops you?

I would show the formula and the mask, and I would refuse a heatmap labeled as the reason for a refund. What stops a looser UI is the absence of that product’s own evaluation. Check it before you call a map the reason; faithfulness varies by model and by task. Check the serving stack for cache bytes; the size varies with length, layers, precision, and batch. [cite:1]
Leaf · Where does a missing policy PDF get mixed in?
It does not. Attention mixes tokens that are already in the window. Pack the PDF or call a tool. The head will not fetch it. [cite:8]
Leaf · Name the license if you serve Llama 4 weights.
The Llama 4 Community License Agreement, effective 5 April 2025. Not MIT. The acceptable-use policy is a separate document the card points at. [cite:9]
09Lab
No API key. Paper, or the sampling lab’s spirit: numbers only.

items: Prerequisite: T1-R01. You can say what a logit is.
Compute the toy: q=[1,0], keys [1,0] and [0,1], d_k=2. Write scaled scores and softmax weights to two decimals.
Zero the future key and recompute. The weight on that key is 0.
Write one sentence that separates sampler temperature from the blog’s attention-temperature scaling.
From the Llama 4 card, state Scout’s active parameters, expert count, and context-length field without looking.
Stop. Do not invent a head count for an OpenAI model id. Do not paste 28.4 BLEU into a contact-center slide.

blocks.text: 10Quiz
Recall
Q1. Scaled dot-product attention is:
Reveal
softmax of QK transpose over the square root of d_k, times V. [cite:1]
Apply
Q2. In the toy, d_k is 2 and the raw dots are 1 and 0. What do you divide by?
Reveal
The square root of 2, before softmax. Skipping the scale is a different function. [cite:1]
Apply
Q3. A future key under the causal mask has weight:
Reveal
Zero, because its score was set so softmax assigns it no mass. The paper’s decoder is causal. [cite:1]
Recall
Q4. The 2017 base model’s head count is:
Reveal
8, with d_model 512. Historical. Not a 2026 product constant. [cite:1]
Apply
Q5. A teammate sets gpt-6-astra’s heads to 8 because “transformers have 8.”
Reveal
The models page fetched 2026-10-14 does not publish that width. Refuse the copy. [cite:6]
Recall
Q6. Llama 4 Scout, on the model card:
Reveal
17B active, 109B total, 16 experts, context length 10M, knowledge cutoff August 2024. [cite:2]
Apply
Q7. Someone says Scout was only trained at 10M context.
Reveal

The card’s context field is 10M. The blog says Scout was pre-trained and post-trained with a 256K context, which empowers length generalization, and it names a 10 million token supported context. Keep both. [cite:3]
Recall
Q8. iRoPE, as the blog names it, includes:
Reveal
RoPE on most layers, interleaved layers without positional embeddings, and inference-time temperature scaling of attention. [cite:3]
Apply
Q9. Raising API temperature to 1.4 changes iRoPE’s attention temperature.
Reveal
No. Those are different scales. Chat-completions temperature divides logits and is documented from 0 to 2. [cite:4]
Apply
