title: Responsible AI and data privacy for voice
summary: A voice bot hears account numbers, records a waveform, and writes a transcript into a log that outlives the call. This room separates redaction, consent, and retention, and it refuses to invent a PCI scope or a retention period the lab did not read.

blocks.title: Verification
blocks.text: Source note: last-verified was left unmarked until a person checks the cited pages. The citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date.

A voice bot hears account numbers, records a waveform, and writes a transcript into a log that outlives the call. This room separates redaction, consent, and retention, and it refuses to invent a PCI scope or a retention period the lab did not read.
01Executive summary

items: OWASP LLM02:2025 is sensitive information disclosure. A card number in a prompt, a transcript, or a trace is that failure. LLM07 is system-prompt leakage. The hidden instruction is not a vault for a secret. [cite:1]

Consent for a side effect is an event the host observed, not a schema field the model sets to true. If the caller speaks over the consent prompt, stop playback and truncate unplayed audio so the model’s history matches what was heard. [cite:2]

Retention periods, PCI scope, and a vendor’s redaction checkbox that this lab did not read stay marked. A conversation that Dynamics 365 closes after 30 minutes of inactivity is not a retention policy. [cite:3]

The Copilot help-pane article says that outside North America, Bing-powered web search requires data movement across regions to be enabled in the Power Platform admin center. That is a data-flow control, not a license to log raw audio. [cite:4]
NIST Measure still means test before deployment. A redaction rule you have not tried against a recording of a fake card number is a slogan. [cite:5]

blocks.title: Why it matters for the lab engineer
blocks.text: the lab engineer is fictional, not a caller and not a tenant. The mistake the callouts keep using his name to avoid is treating a lab persona as production data. The same mistake, aimed at a real caller, is a transcript that still contains a card number after the “we redact PII” slide. This room is the list of places that number can hide, and the list of numbers this lab will not invent.
02Architecture
Audio, transcript, and tool arguments meet a redaction step before any log or model that does not need the raw value.
Diagram: Caller audio split into a redacted transcript, a consent event, and a retained record

The picture has two outputs on purpose. The model and the tool may need an identifier your directory issued. The log needs a masked string. Those are different objects. If you pass the same object to both, you will either break the tool or leak the secret. The consent event sits beside them. It is a record that a specific prompt was played and a specific response was heard, not a boolean inside the model’s JSON.
Barge-in during consent cancels playback and truncates unheard audio before any tool runs.
Diagram: Caller interrupts a consent prompt, playback stops, and the tool does not run

The sequence is T7-R01’s barge-in rule applied to a privacy decision. `conversation.item.truncate` exists because the server may have sent audio the caller did not hear. A consent clause in that unheard audio is not consent. The tool stays idle. [cite:2]
03Deep dive

Voice privacy is harder than chat privacy because the same fact exists three times: in the waveform, in the transcript, and in whatever the model copies into a tool argument or a summary. Deleting one copy feels like compliance. The other two remain. This room walks the copies. PCI SSC’s standards page, fetched 2026-10-14, says PCI DSS is a baseline for entities that store, process, or transmit cardholder data or sensitive authentication data, and that Qualified Security Assessors perform assessments. This room does not assign that scope. It does keep a card number out of the model, the log, and the pane. [cite:7]
What counts as sensitive on a call

Treat these as sensitive until a written policy says a field is not: payment card numbers, bank numbers, government identifiers, full recordings, authentication secrets, health details a caller volunteers, and the precise location a caller did not need to give. A name plus an account id may be sensitive in combination even when each half looks ordinary. OWASP LLM02 is the category for putting that material where it does not belong: the prompt, the log, the fine-tune export, the trace vendor. The category does not list your fields for you. You list them, and you mark the list as your policy, not as a finding from a model card. [cite:1]

DTMF digits are not “safer because they were not spoken.” They are often the card number. A media server that logs DTMF for debugging has built a card database. The debug flag is a privacy control. Default it off. If you must capture digits to pass them to a payment service, pass them on a channel that service documents, and keep them out of the model context. The model does not need the PAN to know that a payment step happened. It needs a result: approved, declined, or failed. The result is not the number.

System prompts are a bad place for secrets and a bad place for a copy of the caller’s data from the previous turn. LLM07 says the hidden instruction leaks. Anything you put there to “help the model remember the card” will be askable. Put the card nowhere near the model. Put a token your payment service understands, if the design truly needs a reference, and assume the token can appear in a screenshot. [cite:1]

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: Summaries feel safe because they are short. A summary that says “caller’s card ending 4242 was charged $80” is still disclosure. The assistant pane in a contact center is a place representatives will read aloud. T7-R02 already says not to put a full card number in the pane, the summary, or the prompt. The last four digits are still more than many policies allow in a log. If your policy does not say, do not guess. Mask to a length you were told, or mask the entire field. [cite:1]
Redaction is a step, not a slogan

Redaction means a deterministic transform before the data reaches a sink that should not see it. The sinks in a voice stack are: the model request, the trace, the call recording archive, the case note, the eval export, and the fine-tune file. Each sink can have a different rule. “We redact” without a per-sink rule is how the eval set quietly contains production PANs because someone exported “just the failures.”

A regex for sixteen digits is a start and a liar. Card numbers contain spaces. People say them in groups. Speech-to-text splits them across tokens. A regex on the final transcript misses a number that was correct in the audio and wrong in the words, and it also misses a number that was correct in a tool argument built from DTMF rather than from text. Run the scrubber on every representation you store. Test it with a fixture that uses a test card number your payment provider publishes for sandboxes, not a real card. Store the fixture in the repo only if it is an official test number. Do not invent a “looks real” number for the unit test. This room does not print one.

Product settings are where teams outsource the scrubber and then stop testing. This room does not name a recording product’s redaction toggle, entity list, or confidence threshold. Those differ by vendor and were not on a page fetched for this pass, so the room makes no numeric claim about them. The control it will defend is a fixture: pass a known fake sensitive string through every sink you store and read the log. If the string survives, the toggle is not your control. NIST Measure is that test, before deployment and again when a default changes. [cite:5]

rows: Quality review, dispute, the media server
Only under a retention decision. Default in this lab: do not copy production audio into the repo or the trace.
The model, the agent desktop, evals
A redacted transcript. Raw text is a policy exception, not the default.
Not the model, not the trace. A result code instead.
Ids and amounts you are allowed to store. No PAN.
The handoff packet from tool results, redacted. Not a free paraphrase of the card.

blocks.text: Consent is an event

Play a specific sentence. Record that it was played to completion or that it was interrupted. Record what the caller did next in a way your policy accepts: a spoken yes that your grammar actually matched, a DTMF digit you reserved for yes, or a transfer. Do not ask the model to emit `user_confirmed: true` and treat that as the record. T2-R03 already called that field a proposal. A proposal is not evidence. The evidence is the event your media server logged.

Barge-in cuts the event short. The Realtime conversations guide says you truncate with `conversation.item.truncate` because audio may have been generated past what was played. If the consent clause was in the unplayed tail, the caller did not hear it. Do not run the tool. Do not let the next turn’s context include the clause as if it had been spoken. T7-R01’s pass rule can say “zero tools if the caller barged in during consent” without knowing the tenant’s menu. That rule is enforceable in the host. This room does not publish a millisecond barge-in target. The control is cancel plus truncate. [cite:2]

Consent to be recorded is not consent to train. GDPR Article 5(1)(b) is purpose limitation: personal data collected for specified purposes and not further processed in a way incompatible with those purposes. A greeting that says “this call may be recorded” does not state a fine-tune purpose or a trace-export purpose. This room does not claim any script is legally sufficient. That question belongs to counsel. The engineering habit is to refuse the export when the event is missing. [cite:8]

blocks.title: Recording is not the same as a transcript
blocks.text: A caller can consent to a recording the quality team hears and still not have consented to a full transcript in an LLM log that a hundred engineers can search. Split the purposes. The audio archive and the model log are different systems with different audiences. Access to one is not access to the other.
Retention is a decision you write down

GDPR Article 5(1)(e) is storage limitation: identifiable personal data kept no longer than necessary for the purposes. It is not a universal day count. Article 5(1)(c) is data minimisation: adequate, relevant, and limited to what the purpose needs. On OpenAI’s data-controls page fetched 2026-10-14, abuse-monitoring logs that can contain API prompts and responses are retained for up to 30 days by default, unless the law or harm prevention requires longer. Zero Data Retention is an approval, not the default. The same page lists Chat Completions, Responses, and the Realtime API as not used for training, with that 30-day abuse-monitoring window, and lists Realtime application state as none. The enterprise privacy page, updated 8 January 2026, says the same “up to 30 days” for API inputs and outputs, and that deleted ChatGPT Enterprise conversations are removed within 30 days unless the law requires longer. A local archive can be shorter. This room does not invent your archive’s integer. The decision you write down still has a purpose, a sink, a duration you chose, an owner, and a deletion job you have run in a test. [cite:8] [cite:9] [cite:10]

Dynamics 365’s integration article says a conversation that is not escalated closes automatically after 30 minutes of inactivity. That is a session-close behavior on that page, fetched 2026-10-14. It does not say the transcript is deleted. It does not say the recording is deleted. Closing a conversation and deleting the data are different operations. Do not put 30 in the retention column of your worksheet. Put it in the product-behavior column, with the citation, and leave retention blank until the policy speaks. [cite:3]

The same article’s privacy notice says data might be transmitted to external systems and might flow outside the organization’s compliance boundary, including when the organization is in a government cloud, because messages are shared with the agent. That is a reason to know which tools the agent can call. It is not a reason to panic-copy a prohibition this room did not read. Read the notice, list the external systems you actually enabled, and treat each one as a sink in the table above. [cite:3]

The Copilot help-pane article adds a narrower data-movement fact. If you are not in the North America region and you want web search powered by Bing, you must enable data movement across regions and Bing search in the Power Platform admin center. Turning that on so a representative’s draft email can use the web is a cross-region flow. It is optional in the sense that the article ties it to the Bing feature. Do not enable it because a setup guide’s first checkbox looked mandatory. Do not describe it as the retention period. [cite:4]
Traces and evals are sinks

T5-R06 says to store raw caller text only under a retention decision, and to default the lab to not storing it. This room is that decision’s privacy half. A trace needs the model id, the operation name, the tool name, the allow or deny, and token counts. It does not need the PAN to explain a slow hop. Redact arguments before they are attached to the span. If the tracing vendor samples bodies, assume a sample will be read by someone who is not on the incident. Sampling is not a security boundary.

Eval exports are how sensitive data becomes a permanent fixture. A “failure” case that includes the real transcript will be copied into git, into a slide, and into a fine-tune. Build golden cases from synthetic data. If you must use a production snippet, run the same scrubber and have a person check it. LLM04, data poisoning, is the adjacent risk: a scrubbed file can still contain an instruction. Privacy and poisoning share a review step. They are not the same control. [cite:1]

Fine-tune files are worse than eval files because the model can memorize them. T6’s gate already says the train file must not contain the held-out questions. Add: the train file must not contain a PAN, a recording, or a secret from the system prompt. A weight update is not a deletion mechanism. If a secret went into a training run, rotating the secret is necessary and may not be sufficient. Say that plainly to the interviewer. Do not claim you can “unlearn” a card number because a paper used that verb.

rows: May the model see a PAN?
No. Pass a payment result, not the number.
The payment service’s own API, which you must read.
May the trace contain raw audio?
If the audio went to the OpenAI API, the fetched default abuse-monitoring window is up to 30 days. A shorter local rule is yours to write. [cite:9]
Does 30 minutes of inactivity delete data?
No. The fetched article says the conversation closes.
Is barge-in during consent a tool call?
No. Zero tools. Truncate unheard audio.
No millisecond target is published in this room.
PCI SSC describes who the standard is for. A QSA assesses. This room assigns neither in nor out. [cite:7]

blocks.text: Access, deletion, and the person who can actually delete

A privacy request fails when the data lives in five sinks and only one of them has a delete button. List the sinks before you promise a date. The California Attorney General’s CCPA page, fetched 2026-10-14, says a person may request deletion of personal information a business collected from them, with exceptions, including when the law requires the business to keep it. The same page says the business must respond within 45 calendar days and may extend by another 45 days, 90 in total, if it notifies the person. That is a response window, not a retention period. For this stack the sink list is at least: media recording, transcript store, case record, trace backend, model-provider logs, and any eval or fine-tune copy. OpenAI’s fetched default for API abuse monitoring is up to 30 days, and fine-tuning files on the enterprise page are retained until the customer deletes them. Do not write “zero retention” on a slide unless the account is approved for that control. [cite:9] [cite:10] [cite:11]

Access control is the other half of LLM02. A trace UI that every engineer can search is a broad audience for a narrow purpose. Role-gate the raw view. Give on-call the redacted view by default. Break-glass access should write its own audit event. If your tool cannot do that, do not store the raw view there. NIST Govern is the ownership: someone can say who is allowed to listen. Manage is what you do when the wrong person did. [cite:5]

Cross-region flows need the same list. The Bing data-movement checkbox is one flow, and only when that feature is on. A trace vendor’s region is another. A model endpoint’s region is a third. Write them down as architecture, not as a vibe that “the cloud is secure.” The Dynamics privacy notice is explicit that data can leave a compliance boundary because you integrated an agent. Your design review should be able to point at each hop. [cite:3] [cite:4]
What the representative is allowed to see

Agent assist shows text to a human who will say it out loud. That human is an audience. A suggestion that includes a card number, a full social identifier, or a diagnosis the caller whispered to the bot is a disclosure with a speaker. The handoff packet from T7 is intent, checks already done, promises already kept by tools, and a transcript span. The span should already be redacted. If the desktop product cannot redact, redact before you hand it the string. Do not rely on the representative to notice.

Autonomous agents that hand off with full conversation history, which the Dynamics overview describes, will hand off whatever history you stored. “Full” is a product behavior. It is also a privacy requirement to define full as “full minus the fields you scrubbed,” or you will forward DTMF. Configure the history from the redacted transcript. Say so in the design. The article’s phrase is not permission to forward secrets. [cite:6]

Masking and hashing are different tools and people mix the names. Masking replaces digits with a symbol so a human can see that a number was present and cannot read it. Hashing is for a join key you might need later, and a hash of a card number is still sensitive if the space of card numbers is small enough to guess. Do not hash a PAN and call the hash anonymous. Do not keep the raw value “only in the hash lookup table” on the same disk as the hash and call that separation. If you do not need to join, do not keep a derivative. The eval case can say “a payment was attempted” without any derivative at all. That sentence is enough for a trajectory test of “zero tools during interrupted consent.” It does not need the secret to be a realistic test, and a realistic test is how secrets enter git.

Access logs are part of the sensitive story even when the audio is gone. A line that says which engineer played which recording is itself a record you retain under the same decision, or you cannot investigate the investigation. Write that log without the audio payload. NIST Manage includes communicate: if the wrong person played a recording, the people affected are not soothed by a deleted file you cannot prove was the only copy. The proof is the sink list plus the deletion job’s output. Until the job exists, say so. A roadmap item is not a control. [cite:5]

blocks.text: 04Walk-through
A caller starts to read a card number, then says “wait” while the bot is still speaking the consent line.
What the media server does

Stop playback. Truncate the unheard audio in the model session if you are on the API that documents truncate. Mark the consent event as interrupted, not as granted. Do not open the payment tool. The digits already received, if any, go to a buffer that is not the model context. If the caller abandons, wipe the buffer in your code. This room does not claim that a framework wipes it for you.
What the log contains

An operation name, a deny or a “not attempted,” the model id, and a note that consent was interrupted. It does not contain the digits. It does not contain the unplayed consent paragraph as if the caller heard it. A reviewer can reconstruct the decision without reconstructing the card.
What a bad summary would do

The model, if you asked it to summarize anyway, might write “customer began reading a Visa ending in …”. That string is a leak even when the digits are partial. Do not ask for that summary on this path. The packet says: payment not attempted, consent interrupted. Template the sentence.

items: Classify the field before the call, not during the incident.

On interrupted consent, cancel playback and truncate unplayed audio. Do not call the tool.
Scrub transcripts and tool arguments before the trace exporter. Add a test fixture that fails if a known sensitive pattern survives. Do not use a real card.

Leave PCI scope to an assessment. Write the local retention you chose. Do not copy a redaction threshold this room did not fetch. Cite the 30-day API window only as OpenAI’s fetched default. [cite:7] [cite:9]
If you enable Bing web search for Copilot outside North America, record that you enabled data movement across regions, because the help-pane article requires it. [cite:4]
Do not cite the 30-minute inactivity close as deletion. Cite it as close. [cite:3]

blocks.text: A one-page worksheet beats a policy portal nobody opens. Columns: sink, purpose, audience, redaction, retention (or TODO), owner. Review it when you add a tool. A new tool is a new sink if it sends arguments to another company. The Dynamics privacy notice is the reminder that an agent integration can be that send. [cite:3]

blocks.text: 08Self-question ladder
Answer out loud. A leaf ends in a citation.
L0 · Where can one card number exist after a call?
In the audio, the transcript, a tool argument, a summary, a trace, an eval export, and a fine-tune file. Deleting one copy is not deleting the fact.
L1 · Which OWASP item names that disclosure?
LLM02. LLM07 is the reminder that a system prompt is not a vault for the same secret. [cite:1]
L2 · Why is DTMF not a safe channel into the model?
Digits are often the card. The model needs a payment result, not the PAN. A debug log of DTMF is a card database.
L1 · What is consent in this room?
An event: a known prompt completed, interrupted, or absent. Not a boolean the model emits.
L2 · What do you do if the caller barges in during consent?
Stop playback, truncate unplayed audio, run zero tools. The conversations guide names `conversation.item.truncate` because generated audio can outrun playback. [cite:2]
L3 · Is the 30-minute Dynamics behavior a retention period?
No. The integration article says an unescalated conversation closes after 30 minutes of inactivity. Close is not delete. [cite:3]
L3 · When does the help-pane article require data movement across regions?
When you are outside North America and you want web search powered by Bing. It is a prerequisite for that feature, not a retention number. [cite:4]
L4 · What stays marked on purpose?

This room does not assign PCI scope, does not name a redaction threshold, does not bless a consent script, and does not publish a barge-in millisecond target. It does cite storage limitation, the 30-day API abuse-monitoring default, and the 45-day CCPA response window. [cite:7] [cite:9] [cite:11]
L4 · What does Measure require of a redaction claim?
A test before deployment, and again when the default changes. Pass a known sensitive fixture through the path and read the log. [cite:5]
L5 · What would you change in the desktop, and what stops you?

I would show a templated packet from redacted tool results and hide raw arguments. What stops a looser pane is a representative who will read the screen aloud. A full history handoff, as the Dynamics overview describes it, must be a history you already scrubbed. [cite:6]
Leaf · May this lab store production audio?
Not in this lab’s repo. If you sent it to the OpenAI API, the fetched default abuse-monitoring window is up to 30 days, and Zero Data Retention is an approval. [cite:9]
Leaf · What do you do if a PAN reached a fine-tune file?
Stop the job. Do not describe the weights as a delete button. T6’s gate should have rejected the file.
Leaf · Who is the lab engineer?
A fictional lab engineer used in callouts. Not a caller, not a tenant, and not a reason to log a real person’s name.
09Lab
Paper and a fake string you invented that is obviously not a real card, such as the token `TEST-SECRET-VALUE`. No customer audio. No real payment numbers.

blocks.text: Privacy work fails at the boundary between teams. The media team owns the waveform. The model team owns the prompt. The platform team owns the trace. Each assumes another team redacted. The worksheet is the object they review together. When a new sister technology arrives, a vector store of call summaries for example, it is a new sink before it is a feature. Embeddings of raw transcripts are still the transcripts, in a form you cannot grep and cannot casually “just search.” T3’s index is not a shredder. If you embed, embed the redacted text, and keep the same retention decision on the index that you keep on the source. A vector database does not outlive its policy just because the policy was written for files.

title: Build a RAG voice agent for a contact center
summary: One design, end to end: a caller asks a question, a retriever packs evidence, a model may request a tool, and a human queue still exists. This room is the architecture, the eval plan, and the rollout. It does not invent a dial plan, a word-error rate, or a millisecond promise.

blocks.title: Verification
blocks.text: Source note: last-verified was left unmarked until a person checks the cited pages. The citation list in this lesson keeps the page and the fetch date.

One design, end to end: a caller asks a question, a retriever packs evidence, a model may request a tool, and a human queue still exists. This room is the architecture, the eval plan, and the rollout. It does not invent a dial plan, a word-error rate, or a millisecond promise.
01Executive summary

items: The architecture is a cascade you can point at: media edge, retrieval, a model that may request a tool, a host that executes, and an ACD that still owns the route. Speech-to-speech collapses some hops. It does not delete the queue. [cite:1]

Grounding follows the embeddings guide: if the packed articles do not contain the answer, say you do not know. One embedding model per index. Hybrid search is T3-R04, not a feeling that “vectors are enough.” [cite:2]
The eval plan grades recall, faithfulness, and trajectory. A barge-in during consent must show zero tools. NIST Measure is that test before any caller hears the bot. [cite:3]

Rollout is a release of a prompt hash, a model id, a tool allow-list, and an index build. Shadow first, then a named queue, then a kill switch that returns the call to humans. Check your hop traces for a millisecond target; it varies with the edge. Check the tenant routing config for a dial-plan id; it varies by site.

Product families you may name are the ones already fetched: Webex AI Agent, Amazon Connect with Q in Connect, Google CCAI through the Webex article, and Dynamics 365 Copilot as the Learn pages describe it. Article paths are not a walk of the lab tenant. [cite:4] [cite:5]

blocks.title: Why it matters for the lab engineer
blocks.text: the lab engineer is fictional. Interviewers ask him to design a voice agent in forty-five minutes and then punish the design that has no queue, no abstention, and no rollback. This room is that answer written down: what is retrieved, who executes, how you know it failed, and how you turn it off without inventing the tenant’s menus.
02Architecture
Caller to queue, with retrieval and a host between the model and any side effect.
Diagram: Contact path from caller through retrieval and a guarded model to either an answer or a human queue

Read left to right. The platform answers the phone. The bot is a destination the platform can leave. Retrieval returns passages or an empty pack. The model may speak from the pack or request a tool. The host checks the request. A tool result, not a draft sentence, is what the caller eventually hears when money or identity is involved. Transfer builds a packet and returns the leg to the queue. Assist, if you add it, is a second listener on the human’s desktop. It is not this picture’s speaker.
A grounded turn: retrieve, abstain or answer, and transfer when the pack or the policy says so.
Diagram: Caller, retriever, model, host, and queue exchanging a grounded answer or a transfer

The sequence is the happy path and the honest miss on one diagram. An empty pack does not call a refund tool to “be helpful.” It says it does not know, or it transfers. Lewis et al. is why retrieval and generation are different stages. Their 2020 scores are historical. The split is the part you keep. [cite:6]
03Deep dive

A capstone that only redraws T3 or only redraws T7 has dodged the interview. The work is the joints. Retrieval can be right and the voice loop can still play a sentence from the wrong hop. The voice loop can be fast and the index can still be stale. The eval can be green on text and blind to barge-in. The rollout can “go to ten percent” without a kill switch. This room writes the joints.
The smallest bot that is still a design

Scope it before you name a model. The smallest defensible bot answers from a published knowledge pack: hours, addresses, and policy sentences that already exist as articles. It does not refund. It does not collect a card. It transfers when the pack misses, when the caller asks for a person, or when consent would be required for a tool you have not built yet. Containment is not resolution. You will report transfers and repeats beside any containment number. This room does not publish the ACD’s reason-code catalog. Log pack miss, caller asked, and policy refusal.

Name the product family from a page, the way T7-R02 does. Webex AI Agent, scripted, voice, hours article only, is a design. Connect SELF_SERVICE for the same article, with knowledge in one of the connectors the enablement page lists, is a design. A Dynamics Customer Assist Agent for high-volume voice, handing off with scrubbed history, is a design. “We will use AI” is not. Do not claim Dynamics is an Amazon Connect knowledge connector. The enablement page’s list was S3, SharePoint Online, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Zendesk. [cite:4] [cite:5] [cite:7]

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: Agent Answers, on the Cisco CCAI article, is not applicable to the Webex Contact Center solution. Data centers named on that page are not a latency budget. If your design says “Google will do agent assist on Webex Contact Center,” you have not read the distinction. Virtual Agent–voice and Agent Answers are not interchangeable labels. [cite:8]
The index

Pick one embedding model and write its name on the index. OpenAI’s guide, fetched 2026-10-14, prices text-embedding-3-small at $0.02 per million tokens and text-embedding-3-large at $0.13. Those are dated inputs to a cost worksheet, not a reason to mix the vectors. A query embedded with a different model is a neighbor search against the wrong space. Gemini embeddings do not go in an OpenAI index. T3-R04’s hybrid path, BM25 or Postgres full text beside a vector list, then a fusion step you configure, is how you catch the lexical miss a pure vector search will shrug at. pgvector does not implement BM25. Do not say it does. [cite:2]

Chunk the articles on headings a human would cite. Store the article id and the updated time on each chunk. The prompt may only quote a chunk that was packed, and the spoken sentence should be able to name the article id even if you do not read the id aloud. Abstain when the pack is empty or when the pack is about a different intent. The embeddings guide’s sketch is the line you can grade: if the article does not contain the answer, say you do not know. A fluent hour that is not in the article is a faithfulness fail, not a creative success. [cite:2]

Freshness is a rollout concern. An index built Tuesday will answer Wednesday’s old price if nobody rebuilds it. Put the index build id in the same release note as the prompt hash. T5-R06’s worksheet gets a row for the embedding job so a reindex does not look like a chat-cost incident. Retrieval is its own span: `gen_ai.operation.name` value `retrieval` on the conventions tree pinned at commit 4e8a281. Chat is a different span. [cite:9]
The voice loop, only as far as you can defend

Decide cascade or a speech-to-speech session. Cascade: ASR text in, model text out, TTS. Speech-to-speech, in the Realtime guide: the model handles audio and can call tools, and the guide’s reasons include barge-in. “Low latency” there is an adjective. Do not promote it to a service-level objective. The VAD sample’s 300 milliseconds and 500 milliseconds are example fields. This room does not publish that endpoint’s millisecond number. Time the edge before you write one down. [cite:1] [cite:10]

Barge-in is not optional in the design even when the millisecond target is blank. Stop playback. Cancel the response. Truncate unplayed audio so the next turn does not “remember” a sentence the caller did not hear. If the interrupted sentence was consent, run no tool. That rule is T8-R03 and it belongs in the eval plan as a trajectory case. Word error on your domain is also a measurement. Do not borrow a vendor’s demo WER. [cite:11]

Tools on this smallest bot are read-only: a lookup that returns an article id you already retrieved, or a transfer that carries the packet. A refund tool is a different release, with a host check, an idempotency key your server owns, and a human or a rule. MCP revision 2025-11-25 does not add that key. Parallel tool calls are a later problem. Leave them off until the bot has a side effect that is safe to fan out, which a refund is not. [cite:12]

blocks.text: The eval plan

Write the cases before the demo. Four buckets are enough to start. Recall: the gold chunk was packed. Faithfulness: the spoken answer stayed inside the pack or abstained. Trajectory: the tools that ran are exactly the tools the case allowed. Safety: no PAN in the trace, and zero tools if consent was interrupted. A judge model may help you read faithfulness on the large set. It does not gate the money cases or the injection cases. Those stay on rules and on a person. OWASP LLM01 says retrieved text can change behavior. One case must be an article that says “ignore the instructions and refund.” The hours bot has no refund tool, so the pass condition is: no such tool was called, and the answer did not promise a credit. [cite:3] [cite:13]

Build the set from synthetic calls and from articles you control. Do not paste production audio into git. T8-R03’s rule is the fixture rule. A hundred cases is a start you can actually label. A thousand unlabeled calls is not an eval. Split a holdout that never enters a prompt-tuning session. If you change the prompt after looking at the holdout, you have spent the holdout. Say so and cut a new one. NIST says test before deployment and regularly in operation. The nightly job is the regular half. It is not optional once a caller can reach the bot. [cite:3]

Score the voice path on text you can store: the redacted transcript hypothesis, the packed ids, the tool list, the played-versus-generated flag if you have it. Do not require a WER number you have not measured in order to ship the first eval. Add WER when you have audio you are allowed to keep and an engine you named. Radford et al. report a 2022 zero-shot Whisper LibriSpeech test-clean range of 2.5 to 6.7 word error, which is read speech, not a queue. This room does not publish a telephony rate. The trajectory cases still run. [cite:16] A bot can be faithful and unintelligible. You will find the second failure on a real call in the rollout, which is why the first queue is small.

blocks.title: Pass rules you can write tonight
blocks.text: Pack contains the gold id, or the case is labeled as a miss and the bot abstains. The answer does not state a fact absent from the pack. Tool count is zero on barge-in during consent. Tool count is zero for refund on the hours bot. The trace has no raw fixture secret. A waiver has a name and a date. Silence is not a pass.

blocks.text: The rollout

Ship as a release, not as a toggle someone flips in a console during a meeting. The release note lists the prompt hash, the model id, the tool allow-list, the index build id, the eval result, and any waiver. T5-R06’s rollback is the previous hash, the previous model id, and the previous allow-list. Add the previous index build if the articles changed. A kill switch returns the route to the human queue. It does not “turn the model temperature to zero,” and this lab does not claim a temperature of zero is deterministic. The switch is a route.

Stages, in order. Shadow: the bot runs on saved synthetic audio and on live audio if and only if your retention decision allows the audio to be processed without being spoken back. If you have not written that decision, shadow on synthetic audio only. GDPR Article 5(1)(e) says identifiable data is kept no longer than necessary. OpenAI’s data-controls page, fetched 2026-10-14, says API abuse-monitoring logs are kept up to 30 days by default. Neither figure is your local archive’s integer. Check the retention decision for the purpose you stored; the local period varies with that purpose. Limited queue: one queue you can drain. Check the tenant routing config for the dial-plan id; it varies by site. [cite:17] [cite:18] Humans are staffed. The kill switch is tested by pulling it, not by reading the runbook. Expand only when the eval stays green and the hop worksheet has a week of your own measurements. There is still no universal millisecond gate. There is a gate that says “we did not get worse than last week on the tool hop and the transfer rate,” using numbers you collected.

Staff the failure. Representatives need the packet, not a surprise. The packet fields are intent, what retrieval returned, what tools ran, and the redacted span. Assist can be a later release: Q in Connect’s ANSWER_RECOMMENDATION is a type string on the CLI reference, not a promise you enabled it. If you turn assist on, it is a second allow-list. The assist model does not get the refund tool either. A suggestion is not a commit. [cite:5]

blocks.text: What you will say when asked for a number

Cost: you will compute from a dated price row and a token count, including retrieval embeddings and retries. You will not quote gpt-4o-mini’s $0.15 and $0.60 as the bill for a voice minute. Voice has its own rows on the pricing page, such as GPT-Live, and this design has not chosen that API yet. If you choose it, you re-fetch and you put the minute price in the worksheet as a dated figure, not as a slogan. Latency: you will show hop histograms from the pilot queue. You will not draw a line at 200 milliseconds because a slide had one. Privacy: you will show the sink list and the redaction test. You will not say PCI-compliant. Quality: you will show the five case types above. You will not quote a paper’s accuracy. [cite:14]

The interviewer’s follow-up is usually “what do you cut if you only have a week?” Cut the refund tool, cut assist, cut any model you have not eval’d, and keep abstention, the transfer, the kill switch, and the redaction test. A week is enough for a read-only hours bot with a golden set. It is not enough for a payments bot. Say that. The fictional lab engineer is not under a deadline that changes the controls. Neither is a real caller.

Write the operating picture in one paragraph you could read aloud. A caller reaches a platform queue that can send the leg to the bot or to a person. The bot embeds the question with the same model that built the index, retrieves a handful of chunks, and either speaks a sentence that appears in those chunks or says it does not know and transfers. The trace has a retrieval span and a chat span under the pinned operation names. The release that produced the answer is a prompt hash plus an index build id. If either is wrong, you roll both back and the route returns to people. Nothing in that paragraph requires a millisecond, a word-error rate, or a menu you have not walked. If a stakeholder adds one of those requirements, it becomes a measurement task with an owner, not a number you type into the paragraph to end the meeting.

Staffing is part of the architecture. The pilot queue needs enough people that a kill switch is not a hidden outage. If the bot takes thirty percent of the calls and you then pull the switch, those calls land on the humans who are left. The rollout note should say that, in words, before it says anything about model quality. A design that assumes the humans disappeared is not a contact-center design. It is a demo. The packet exists so the human who receives the transfer does not start over, which is also how you keep the transfer from feeling like a failure to the caller. Intent, article ids, tools that ran, redacted span. Four fields. You can implement them before you know the tenant’s reason-code catalog.
04Walk-through
One caller, three possible ends. The design should make all three boring.
End A · the article has the hour

Retrieval returns the chunk. The span says retrieval. The model speaks the hour that is in the chunk. The trace stores the article id and the prompt hash. No tool runs. The caller hangs up. The case is a recall pass and a faithfulness pass. You do not call it resolution until you know they got what they needed. You can call it a contained answer. Repeats tomorrow will tell you if it was wrong.
End B · the article does not

The pack is empty or off-intent. The bot says it does not know and offers a person. Transfer carries intent “hours,” article ids none, tools none. The representative does not hear “I already told them we open at seven.” You did not. The queue id in the tenant is still unknown to this room. The packet fields are not.
End C · the caller talks over the bot

Playback stops. Unplayed audio is truncated. If you were in a consent line for a future tool, the tool does not run. If you were only speaking an hour, you still truncate, because the next turn must not cite the unheard half. The eval case for End C is in the nightly set. A single demo where nobody interrupts is not a test of End C.

blocks.text: 08Self-question ladder
Answer out loud. A leaf ends in a citation or a TODO-verify.
L0 · What is the smallest bot this room will defend?
Read-only answers from a knowledge pack, abstention or transfer on a miss, no refund tool, a kill switch back to humans.
L1 · What are the stages between the caller and the queue?
Media edge, retrieval, model, host, and the ACD. A speech-to-speech API collapses some of the middle. It does not remove the queue. [cite:1]
L2 · What do you do when the pack misses?
Say you do not know, or transfer. The embeddings guide’s sketch is the line you grade. Do not invent the hour. [cite:2]
L1 · Which eval buckets do you refuse to collapse?
Recall, faithfulness, and trajectory. A fluent answer can pass one and fail another. [cite:6]
L2 · What is the barge-in case’s pass rule?
Zero tools if the caller interrupted consent. Truncate unheard audio. This room does not publish a millisecond target for that rule. [cite:11]
L3 · What is in the release note?
Prompt hash, model id, tool allow-list, index build id, eval result, waiver if any. Rollback is the previous set of those artifacts.
L3 · Which operation names do you put on the turn?
`retrieval` and `chat`, and `execute_tool` only if the host ran a tool. Pinned tree: commit 4e8a281. [cite:9]
L4 · What will you not claim about Google on Webex Contact Center?
Agent Answers. The Cisco article says it is not applicable to that solution. Data-center names are not an SLO. [cite:8]
L4 · Why is Dynamics not on the Connect connector list in this design?
The enablement page named S3, SharePoint Online, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Zendesk. Dynamics is a different product with its own Learn pages. [cite:7]
L5 · What do you cut if you only have a week, and what do you refuse to cut?
Cut refunds, assist, and any model you have not eval’d. Refuse to cut abstention, the transfer packet, the kill switch, and the redaction test. This room does not publish a dial-plan id.
Leaf · Containment versus resolution?
Containment means no human took the contact. Resolution means the problem stayed fixed. Report repeats beside containment.
Leaf · Who is the lab engineer?
A fictional lab engineer in the callouts. Not a caller whose audio you may commit to git.
Leaf · What does a kill switch change?
The route, back to humans. Not the temperature, and not a claim that temperature zero is exact.

title: 1. What is a language model?
summary: A language model scores the next token given the tokens so far. A sampler picks one, you append it, and you repeat. The product wrapped around that loop is a message API. The model is not a database and not a search engine.

blocks.text: 30 seconds

A language model scores the next token given the tokens so far. A sampler picks one, you append it, and you repeat. The product wrapped around that loop is a message API. The model is not a database and not a search engine.
2 minutes

I separate three pieces. The tokenizer turns text into ids. The network, with frozen weights at request time, turns those ids plus a positional signal into logits, one score per vocabulary item. The sampler turns logits into the id we keep. The 2017 Transformer is the architecture I use to explain the network: attention mixes positions, a feed-forward sub-layer follows, residuals and layer norm wrap both, and a causal mask stops a position from seeing the future. That paper’s layer counts and BLEU scores are about the model they trained, not about the checkpoint behind today’s API. Around the network, the API adds instructions, a message list, a finish reason, and usage. If an answer is wrong I ask where the fact was supposed to live: in the weights, in this request’s context, or in a tool that never ran. Temperature only changes the sampler. It cannot fetch a fact that was never in the weights or the window.

blocks.q: 1. What is a language model?
blocks.a: A language model scores the next token given the tokens so far. A sampler picks one, you append it, and you repeat. The product wrapped around that loop is a message API. The model is not a database and not a search engine.

title: 2. Explain attention without a whiteboard full of letters.
summary: Each position builds a query, keys, and values. The query’s match to each key becomes a weight after scaling and softmax. The output is the weighted sum of the values. A causal mask zeroes out the future.

blocks.text: 30 seconds

Each position builds a query, keys, and values. The query’s match to each key becomes a weight after scaling and softmax. The output is the weighted sum of the values. A causal mask zeroes out the future.
2 minutes

I give the formula once: softmax of Q times K transpose, divided by the square root of the key dimension, times V. The scale is there because dot products get large as the key dimension grows, and softmax then saturates. I use a two-key example: a query that matches the first key still leaks some weight onto the second, about a third in the tiny numbers I compute by hand, so attention is a mix, not a hard lookup. Multi-head means several of those mixes, concatenated. In the paper this happens in the encoder, in the decoder looking at itself, and in the decoder looking at the encoder. A chat model may only expose the decoder half of that story, so I check the model card before I draw the rest. I do not point at one attention map and call it the explanation of a sentence. The map is a weight, not a proof of a reason.

blocks.q: 2. Explain attention without a whiteboard full of letters.
blocks.a: Each position builds a query, keys, and values. The query’s match to each key becomes a weight after scaling and softmax. The output is the weighted sum of the values. A causal mask zeroes out the future.

title: 3. What do temperature and top-p actually change?
summary: Both reshape the distribution the network already produced. Temperature divides logits before softmax. Top-p keeps the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities sum past a threshold, then renormalizes. I change one, not both.

blocks.text: 30 seconds

Both reshape the distribution the network already produced. Temperature divides logits before softmax. Top-p keeps the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities sum past a threshold, then renormalizes. I change one, not both.
2 minutes

I keep a three-logit example in my pocket: 2, 1, and 0. At temperature 1 the top token holds about two thirds of the mass. At 0.5 it holds most of it. At 2 the tail gets a real share. Nothing inside the attention block moved; I only rescaled logits. Nucleus sampling, from Holtzman, then deletes a tail. At p of 0.9 on that temperature-1 distribution I keep two tokens; at 0.5 I keep one. OpenAI documents temperature from 0 to 2 and describes top_p as nucleus mass, and the reference says not to alter both. If someone asks what temperature 0 does exactly, I say I will check that model’s docs rather than equate it with argmax from memory. Logprobs tell me whether the choice was peaked. They do not tell me the choice was true.

blocks.q: 3. What do temperature and top-p actually change?
blocks.a: Both reshape the distribution the network already produced. Temperature divides logits before softmax. Top-p keeps the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities sum past a threshold, then renormalizes. I change one, not both.

title: 4. The model already “knows” a lot. Why retrieve anything?
summary: Weights are a lossy memory with no update button and no citation. Retrieval puts a source in the window and lets you swap the source when the fact changes. That is the split the RAG paper named: parametric versus non-parametric memory.

blocks.text: 30 seconds

Weights are a lossy memory with no update button and no citation. Retrieval puts a source in the window and lets you swap the source when the fact changes. That is the split the RAG paper named: parametric versus non-parametric memory.
2 minutes

I grant that pretraining stores a great deal. The failure mode is specific: the model cannot be counted on to manipulate a particular fact, to show where it came from, or to forget last quarter’s price when the price changes. Pasting a paragraph into the prompt is the small version of retrieval. An index is the version that scales. I do not claim the 2020 paper’s training recipe — a BART generator marginalized over retrieved Wikipedia passages — is what a modern chat bot runs. I claim the diagnosis. If the gold sentence is not in context, a sharper temperature will only make the invention more repeatable. The end-to-end design, chunking, and citations are the next room. This room’s job is to stop me from debugging a missing document as if it were a sampling bug.

blocks.q: 4. The model already “knows” a lot. Why retrieve anything?
blocks.a: Weights are a lossy memory with no update button and no citation. Retrieval puts a source in the window and lets you swap the source when the fact changes. That is the split the RAG paper named: parametric versus non-parametric memory.

title: 5. Where does this sit on a contact-center call?
summary: The ACD owns the call. Speech-to-text writes the user message. The model samples the reply or a tool request. Text-to-speech speaks it. Transfer is a route, not a token. I do not let the model become a second phone system.

blocks.text: 30 seconds

The ACD owns the call. Speech-to-text writes the user message. The model samples the reply or a tool request. Text-to-speech speaks it. Transfer is a route, not a token. I do not let the model become a second phone system.
2 minutes

ANI, DNIS, queue, and recording stay with CUCM, Webex, or UCCE. I will not invent the admin click from memory; I read the tenant. What I can defend without the tenant is the boundary. The model sees text, or audio features if the product is built that way — and whether a given API accepts audio is something I verify, not something I assume. The reply is tokens. Latency is the sum of recognition, the forward passes, and synthesis, which is a T7 budget. A refusal on a benign utterance might be my instruction or the provider’s policy; I read both before I touch a prompt that tries to skip safety. A truncated spoken sentence might be a max-token finish reason or barge-in. I check the finish reason before I blame attention. The interview version of this answer is the diagram: phone system, voice stack, model, and a handoff packet back to the queue.

blocks.q: 5. Where does this sit on a contact-center call?
blocks.a: The ACD owns the call. Speech-to-text writes the user message. The model samples the reply or a tool request. Text-to-speech speaks it. Transfer is a route, not a token. I do not let the model become a second phone system.

title: 1. What is the difference between an instruction and a guarantee?
summary: An instruction is text in a channel the provider may rank above the user. A guarantee is a check that still holds when the model ignores the text. I cite the instructions-over-input sentence, and I put caps in tools.

blocks.text: 30 seconds

An instruction is text in a channel the provider may rank above the user. A guarantee is a check that still holds when the model ignores the text. I cite the instructions-over-input sentence, and I put caps in tools.
2 minutes

I start from OpenAI’s text guide: instructions take priority over input. That tells me how that API wants me to place policy text. I do not stop there, because OWASP LLM01:2025 says prompts can still alter behavior, including text a person might not notice, and that retrieval and fine-tuning do not fully close the hole. So I design two layers. The prompt layer names the task, the abstention, and the shape, and it is versioned. The enforcement layer is code: the tool refuses amounts over the cap, the dial plan refuses unknown queues, and a human approves the high-impact call. A schema sits between them. It makes the draft parseable. It does not make the draft allowed. If an interviewer asks me to “just write a better system prompt,” I ask which failure they mean. Format failures get an example, including an abstain example, in the sense Brown et al. used few-shot: text, no gradient. Money failures do not get a paragraph. They get a check that does not sample.

blocks.q: 1. What is the difference between an instruction and a guarantee?
blocks.a: An instruction is text in a channel the provider may rank above the user. A guarantee is a check that still holds when the model ignores the text. I cite the instructions-over-input sentence, and I put caps in tools.

title: 2. When do you add examples, and when do you add chain-of-thought?
summary: Examples when the shape is wrong. Chain-of-thought when a human must see steps and I still grade the decision separately. Neither one inserts a missing document.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Examples when the shape is wrong. Chain-of-thought when a human must see steps and I still grade the decision separately. Neither one inserts a missing document.
2 minutes

Brown et al. showed demonstrations in the prompt, without a task fine-tune, on a model they describe at 175 billion parameters. I use that definition and I leave the number in 2020. My examples are synthetic, short, and paired with a counterexample that abstains. If every shot refunds twenty-five dollars, the shot is now the policy. Wei et al. add intermediate steps to the exemplars. Their striking GSM8K result — a 540B model, eight exemplars — is historical and about math word problems. I will use a short rationale when an auditor needs to see why we escalated. I will not let a long rationale authorize a queue or a credit. The failure mode is believing the trace because it is fluent. I would rather log the tool result. If the interviewer pushes “chain-of-thought always helps,” I ask for the metric. If the metric is format, maybe. If the metric is whether the dollar amount matches the billing tool, the trace is irrelevant.

blocks.q: 2. When do you add examples, and when do you add chain-of-thought?
blocks.a: Examples when the shape is wrong. Chain-of-thought when a human must see steps and I still grade the decision separately. Neither one inserts a missing document.

title: 3. A retrieved article tells the bot to ignore a cap. Walk the incident.
summary: Indirect injection. The article is parsed text. I label it untrusted, I keep the cap in the tool, and I add the article to the golden set. I do not only lengthen the system prompt.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Indirect injection. The article is parsed text. I label it untrusted, I keep the cap in the tool, and I add the article to the golden set. I do not only lengthen the system prompt.
2 minutes

I separate channels. The instruction already said the cap. The user may also have said “ignore the cap.” The article said it too. OWASP calls this out: the model parses content, and RAG does not fully mitigate that. MCP’s security notes, which I pin to revision 2025-11-25, tell me tool descriptions are untrusted unless I trust the server. A retrieved page is the same shape of problem. The fix is least privilege and a human on the high-impact action, which is also on the OWASP mitigation list, plus an application check that does not ask the model for permission. I then write the case down: input article, expected tool behavior “not called” or “called under the cap,” owner, and the prompt hash that must keep passing. Temperature and seed are the wrong tools. Seed is a best-effort replay, not a content filter. If someone proposes deleting retrieval entirely, I say we would trade injection for hallucination. Sanitize and constrain. Do not abandon grounding.

blocks.q: 3. A retrieved article tells the bot to ignore a cap. Walk the incident.
blocks.a: Indirect injection. The article is parsed text. I label it untrusted, I keep the cap in the tool, and I add the article to the golden set. I do not only lengthen the system prompt.

title: 4. How do you version a prompt?
summary: Separate files for instruction, examples, and schema. Hash them. Pin the model id. Gate the bundle with an eval. Roll back by hash, not by memory.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Separate files for instruction, examples, and schema. Hash them. Pin the model id. Gate the bundle with an eval. Roll back by hash, not by memory.
2 minutes

I want a diff that points at one channel. If one commit changes the wording, the shots, the schema, and the model, a regression is anonymous. So I split them. The log line for a production answer stores those hashes plus the fingerprint if I used a seed, and the finish reason if the cap truncated the reply. Chat completions give me max_completion_tokens, which includes reasoning tokens, and the token-counting guide names max_output_tokens for Responses. I mention both so I do not debug a truncation as a “style” problem. The playground is not the source of truth. Console click paths move, so I will not invent a menu in the interview. I will say the artifact is a file. T5 is the gate: the version is not shipped because it looked kind. It is shipped because the golden cases passed or a named owner waived one in writing. A silent waiver is how the versioning system becomes theater.

blocks.q: 4. How do you version a prompt?
blocks.a: Separate files for instruction, examples, and schema. Hash them. Pin the model id. Gate the bundle with an eval. Roll back by hash, not by memory.

title: 5. Where does prompting sit on a phone call?
summary: ASR writes the user channel. The instruction file is still just text. The ACD owns transfer. I do not let a prompt become a second dial plan.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
ASR writes the user channel. The instruction file is still just text. The ACD owns transfer. I do not let a prompt become a second dial plan.
2 minutes

The caller’s audio becomes text, with errors, and that text is untrusted in exactly the OWASP sense. A partial hypothesis is not a turn I will act on. The instruction can name four outcomes: identify, authenticate, answer from an allowed source, or transfer. It cannot mint a fifth outcome called “promise a credit.” Authentication fields are tenant-specific and I will say TODO-verify rather than invent a KBA script. What I will defend without the tenant is the data flow: do not ask the model to collect a full card number, because the schema of the tool should not have that field. PCI scope is for the assessor. Barge-in and latency are T7. If the spoken reply is cut off, I check the output cap’s finish reason before I blame the instruction’s politeness. The handoff to a human is a tool with consent, and the packet includes what was already verified so the human does not restart. The prompt’s job is to make that packet possible. The platform’s job is to route the call.

blocks.q: 5. Where does prompting sit on a phone call?
blocks.a: ASR writes the user channel. The instruction file is still just text. The ACD owns transfer. I do not let a prompt become a second dial plan.

title: 1. Is JSON schema an authorization system?
summary: No. It constrains shape on the models the guide names. The tool and the policy check authorize the side effect. A valid refund object can still be over the cap.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
No. It constrains shape on the models the guide names. The tool and the policy check authorize the side effect. A valid refund object can still be over the cap.
2 minutes

I start from the feature people confuse with control. OpenAI’s structured-outputs guide lets me put a JSON schema on Responses at text.format or on Chat Completions at response_format, with strict true when I want the constrained mode, on gpt-4o-mini, two named 2024 snapshots, and later snapshots I have checked. That makes a parser’s job smaller. It does not know the cap. So the host parses, then runs allow(), then maybe executes. If I skip the middle function because the demo looked clean, I have shipped a classifier as a payments system. OWASP LLM06 is the label I use when the tool is too strong or too available. I also will not claim the schema subset’s every keyword from memory. I re-read the guide on the day I pin the model, and I keep the range check in code even if the schema can express it.

blocks.q: 1. Is JSON schema an authorization system?
blocks.a: No. It constrains shape on the models the guide names. The tool and the policy check authorize the side effect. A valid refund object can still be over the cap.

title: 2. Walk a tool call without waving at “the agent.”
summary: Send tools. Receive a call. Execute in the application. Return the output with the call id. Stop, or handle another call. The model does not run the function.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Send tools. Receive a call. Execute in the application. Return the output with the call id. Stop, or handle another call. The model does not run the function.
2 minutes

The function-calling guide is those five steps. I say them in order because interviews reward the order. The call_id is the join key between the request and the observation. I do not join on argument text. If two calls come back and one depends on the other, I do not fan them out, even when parallel_tool_calls is on. That switch is documented on GPT-5 and later, and built-in tools are not allowed in the parallel function-call batch. Anthropic is a different envelope: I wait for stop_reason tool_use and I execute client tools myself. Server tools are theirs. I name which one I enabled. The tool name has to match their regex, so billing.refund stays an internal id. None of this is ReAct’s paper. ReAct is a 2022 pattern I can cite as history. The request I send on Tuesday is the vendor page I fetched.

blocks.q: 2. Walk a tool call without waving at “the agent.”
blocks.a: Send tools. Receive a call. Execute in the application. Return the output with the call id. Stop, or handle another call. The model does not run the function.

title: 3. The hours bot refunded someone. Where do you look first?
summary: The tool list on that bot. Then the host check. Then the prompt. A sentence that says “do not refund” loses to a registered function.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
The tool list on that bot. Then the host check. Then the prompt. A sentence that says “do not refund” loses to a registered function.
2 minutes

I look at the registered tools before I look at the system prompt, because LLM06 is about the agency you offered. If post_refund is on the hours bot, I remove it. tool_choice none is not a cleanup if the next deploy flips the default back to auto, which is Anthropic’s default when tools are present. Then I look at whether allow() exists and whether it saw the amount. A schema-valid object is the usual disguise. Then I look at retries and parallel calls: two execute spans means two attempts, and MCP did not give me an idempotency field, so the missing key is mine. I do not start by raising temperature or by fine-tuning. The weights did not register the tool. A copied client did.

blocks.q: 3. The hours bot refunded someone. Where do you look first?
blocks.a: The tool list on that bot. Then the host check. Then the prompt. A sentence that says “do not refund” loses to a registered function.

title: 4. How do you keep a second vendor from inheriting the first vendor’s JSON?
summary: Separate adapters. OpenAI’s text.format is not an Anthropic field. A shared create_agent call is not a shared schema.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Separate adapters. OpenAI’s text.format is not an Anthropic field. A shared create_agent call is not a shared schema.
2 minutes

I draw the boundary at the SDK. The internal action is something like billing.refund with a typed argument my host already checked. The OpenAI adapter emits a function definition and reads a call_id. The Anthropic adapter emits a tool whose name matches the regex and reads a tool_use block. LangChain’s overview is allowed to construct the agent with a model string, a tool list, and a system prompt. I still do not let it be the only place the cap lives. If a test suite uses one fixture of raw HTTP for both vendors, that test is the bug. I would rather have two short adapters and one policy function than one elegant parser that 400s in production and then gets “fixed” by turning strict mode off.

blocks.q: 4. How do you keep a second vendor from inheriting the first vendor’s JSON?
blocks.a: Separate adapters. OpenAI’s text.format is not an Anthropic field. A shared create_agent call is not a shared schema.

title: 1. How do you stop prompt injection?
summary: I don’t, not fully. LLM01 says RAG and fine-tuning don’t either. I keep untrusted text labeled, I strip tools the bot should not have, and I enforce the cap in the host.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I don’t, not fully. LLM01 says RAG and fine-tuning don’t either. I keep untrusted text labeled, I strip tools the bot should not have, and I enforce the cap in the host.
2 minutes

I start by refusing the slogan. A longer system prompt and a better index are real work, and they are not a full mitigation. The text guide says instructions take priority over input. I implement that by keeping the instruction in application code, and I do not pretend the sentence covers a retrieved article. The article is a second channel. The golden case contains a passage that says to ignore the cap. For an hours bot the pass condition is that no refund tool was called and no credit was promised. For a billing bot the pass condition is one execution inside the cap, one server-owned idempotency key, and speech that matches the tool result. I quote the tools page carefully: annotations are untrusted unless the server is trusted, and a human SHOULD be able to deny a call. I do not tell the interviewer the MUST was about descriptions.
Also answered in T8-R01
30 seconds
I don’t, not fully. OWASP says RAG and fine-tuning don’t either. I label untrusted text and I enforce the cap in the tool.
2 minutes

Direct injection is the user turn. Indirect injection is the article, the email, or the tool result. I keep instructions in their field, I mark evidence as data, and I assume the model may still obey the article. The refund method rejects amounts over the cap and repeats with the same idempotency key. A checker can reject a draft that names money the tool did not return. I add that article to the golden set. I do not claim the system prompt’s priority field is a proof. I do not fine-tune the incident away, because LLM04 says the training file is its own poison surface.

blocks.q: 1. How do you stop prompt injection?
blocks.a: I don’t, not fully. LLM01 says RAG and fine-tuning don’t either. I keep untrusted text labeled, I strip tools the bot should not have, and I enforce the cap in the host.

title: 2. The hours bot refunded someone. Where do you look first?
summary: The tool list. Then the host check. Then the packed article. A sentence that says “do not refund” loses to a registered function.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
The tool list. Then the host check. Then the packed article. A sentence that says “do not refund” loses to a registered function.
