I look at the registered tools before I look at the wording, because LLM06 is the agency I offered. If post_refund is on the hours bot, I remove it. tool_choice none is not cleanup, especially where auto is the default once tools are present. Then I look at whether allow() saw the amount or whether it trusted an annotation that said to skip the cap. Then I look at the article that was packed, because indirect injection looks like evidence. Then I look at retries: two execute spans and two ledger lines fail the trajectory even if the last sentence apologizes. The key that would have collapsed them is mine. The changelog since 2025-06-18 did not add it. I do not start by fine-tuning. LLM01 already told me that will not fully mitigate the case I just watched.

blocks.q: 2. The hours bot refunded someone. Where do you look first?
blocks.a: The tool list. Then the host check. Then the packed article. A sentence that says “do not refund” loses to a registered function.

title: 3. What does SEP-1577 change about who runs the tool?
summary: It doesn’t. The line adds tools and toolChoice parameters on sampling. The host still mediates. The model still does not execute.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
It doesn’t. The line adds tools and toolChoice parameters on sampling. The host still mediates. The model still does not execute.
2 minutes

I quote the changelog item in full: “Add tool calling support to sampling via tools and toolChoice parameters.” Then I say what I will not add. It does not execute the tool. It does not add an idempotency key. The protocol version I will name is 2025-11-25, because that is the current version the versioning page stated on the fetch this lab did. A missing MCP-Protocol-Version header assumes 2025-03-26, and an unsupported version is HTTP 400. I mention that only to separate the header from the prompt. Sending the right header does not sanitize an article. On the vendor side I keep the same split I already had: OpenAI’s application executes and returns by call_id; Anthropic’s application executes client tools after tool_use; Anthropic executes server tools. SEP-1577 does not move a client tool into the model.

blocks.q: 3. What does SEP-1577 change about who runs the tool?
blocks.a: It doesn’t. The line adds tools and toolChoice parameters on sampling. The host still mediates. The model still does not execute.

title: 4. A schema-valid refund comes back. What do you do with it?
summary: I parse it, then I run the cap. Strict mode made the shape more reliable. It did not authorize the money.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I parse it, then I run the cap. Strict mode made the shape more reliable. It did not authorize the money.
2 minutes

I name the field so the interviewer knows which API I mean. On Responses the schema is text.format with type json_schema and strict true. On Chat Completions it is response_format. The guide names gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, gpt-4o-2024-08-06, and later snapshots. I re-read “later” on the day I pin. The object in the fixture has an amount of four thousand dollars. The example cap is fifty. allow() returns no. I do not call the provider. I do send a tool result on that call_id so the next sentence cannot claim success. I will not join a later result by comparing argument text. If a judge model approved the object, I take the judge off the money gate, because it read the same untrusted passage. The rule stays.

blocks.q: 4. A schema-valid refund comes back. What do you do with it?
blocks.a: I parse it, then I run the cap. Strict mode made the shape more reliable. It did not authorize the money.

title: 1. Design a grounded assistant. Start wherever you want.
summary: I separate ingest from query. Ingest chunks documents, embeds them with a pinned model, and stores vectors with ids and filters. Query embeds the question with that same model, filters, packs a few chunks with ids, and accepts an answer only when every cited id was packed. Otherw

blocks.text: 30 seconds

I separate ingest from query. Ingest chunks documents, embeds them with a pinned model, and stores vectors with ids and filters. Query embeds the question with that same model, filters, packs a few chunks with ids, and accepts an answer only when every cited id was packed. Otherwise it abstains.
2 minutes

I say up front that I am describing retrieve-then-read, not the 2020 paper’s end-to-end marginalization, unless they want that paper. Then I name the objects I persist: document hash, chunk id, embedding model id, dimension, audience. I rank with the distance the embedding provider documents — for the OpenAI guide, cosine — and if I am in Postgres I use pgvector’s cosine distance and a matching HNSW operator class. I keep a token budget so the abstention instruction is not the thing that gets truncated. I log packed ids. Evaluation, which I will only sketch, asks two questions: was the gold chunk retrieved, and did the answer stay inside it. I do not quote a chunk size. I say I will measure recall. I mention hybrid search only for rare strings, because that is the failure pure vectors are bad at, and I cite the README’s suggestion to fuse with full-text rather than a folklore score. Updates are row replacements plus a re-embed, which is the practical form of the paper’s claim that non-parametric memory can be swapped.

blocks.q: 1. Design a grounded assistant. Start wherever you want.
blocks.a: I separate ingest from query. Ingest chunks documents, embeds them with a pinned model, and stores vectors with ids and filters. Query embeds the question with that same model, filters, packs a few chunks with ids, and accepts an answer only when every cited id was packed. Otherwise it abstains.

title: 2. What did the RAG paper contribute that a tutorial often skips?
summary: A probabilistic model. Retrieved documents are latent. RAG-Sequence shares one document across the output. RAG-Token can switch per token. They fine-tuned the query encoder and BART and froze the document index.

blocks.text: 30 seconds

A probabilistic model. Retrieved documents are latent. RAG-Sequence shares one document across the output. RAG-Token can switch per token. They fine-tuned the query encoder and BART and froze the document index.
2 minutes

I give the generator and the retriever their names: BART-large at the size the paper states, 400 million parameters, and DPR as a bi-encoder doing maximum inner-product search. I mention they did not require a labeled “correct document”; the loss is the marginal likelihood of the answer. I mention they kept the document encoder fixed because moving it means rebuilding the index. Then I draw the line: a modern system that stuffs chunks into a frozen chat model is using the diagnosis — parametric memory is not enough — and not the training recipe. If the interviewer wants the recipe, I can talk about the top-k approximation. If they want a design, I switch back to filters, packs, and abstention. I do not recite their 2020 leaderboard as if it were my expected accuracy.

blocks.q: 2. What did the RAG paper contribute that a tutorial often skips?
blocks.a: A probabilistic model. Retrieved documents are latent. RAG-Sequence shares one document across the output. RAG-Token can switch per token. They fine-tuned the query encoder and BART and froze the document index.

title: 3. A retrieval demo looks good in a notebook and bad in production. Where do you look?
summary: I compare the string that was embedded, the filter, the packed ids, and the citation check. Most “model got worse” stories are one of those four.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I compare the string that was embedded, the filter, the packed ids, and the citation check. Most “model got worse” stories are one of those four.
2 minutes

Notebooks query with a typed question and no audience filter. Production queries with an ASR transcript, a locale, and a tenant id. I log the exact query text. I run the same vector in SQL without the filter to see if the filter ate the gold chunk. I confirm the HNSW operator class matches the distance, because a sequential scan or a reversed sort looks like a bad model. I confirm one embedding model id. Then I look at the pack: a correct top-5 that never reaches the prompt is an application bug. Finally I look at whether we displayed an answer that cited nothing. I only retune k or chunking after those checks, and I retune against a golden set, not against the last angry ticket.

blocks.q: 3. A retrieval demo looks good in a notebook and bad in production. Where do you look?
blocks.a: I compare the string that was embedded, the filter, the packed ids, and the citation check. Most “model got worse” stories are one of those four.

title: 4. How do you keep a knowledge bot from leaking across customers?
summary: The filter is a security control. Identity and tenant are predicates on the query, not hints in the prompt. If the predicate is missing, I do not search.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
The filter is a security control. Identity and tenant are predicates on the query, not hints in the prompt. If the predicate is missing, I do not search.
2 minutes

I treat customer-specific text as a different corpus from public help articles. Public articles can be retrieved for any caller in that locale. Account notes require an authenticated identity whose value is bound in the query, not concatenated into a sentence the model might ignore. I still run the citation check. I do not put raw account numbers into the embedding vendor if the contract forbids it — and I say I will read that contract rather than guess. On a contact-center desktop, the agent is authenticated and the caller may not be; those are different filters. The phone system’s recording policy is a separate decision from the retrieval decision. I will not invent the Webex or UCCE field names. I will insist the design has a field.

blocks.q: 4. How do you keep a knowledge bot from leaking across customers?
blocks.a: The filter is a security control. Identity and tenant are predicates on the query, not hints in the prompt. If the predicate is missing, I do not search.

title: 5. When would you not use a vector index?
summary: When the corpus is small enough to put in the prompt, when the question is an exact key lookup, or when you are not allowed to send the text to an embedding API and you have no local model approved.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
When the corpus is small enough to put in the prompt, when the question is an exact key lookup, or when you are not allowed to send the text to an embedding API and you have no local model approved.
2 minutes

A fifty-row status table wants a query by key, not a nearest neighbor. A single policy that fits the window wants the abstention prompt and no index. An error-code lookup wants full-text or an exact match, with vectors only as a supplement — that is the hybrid case, not a reason to start with vectors. If legal has not approved the embedding vendor, the index does not exist yet; a local model is a T6 serving problem with a license to read. I also skip the index when I cannot name the update path. An index nobody can delete from is how last quarter’s price survives. The paper’s contribution, for this answer, is the reminder that the index is memory you must be able to replace.

blocks.q: 5. When would you not use a vector index?
blocks.a: When the corpus is small enough to put in the prompt, when the question is an exact key lookup, or when you are not allowed to send the text to an embedding API and you have no local model approved.

title: 1. What is an agent, and what is MCP?
summary: An agent is a loop: the model requests a tool, my code runs it, the result comes back, and a budget stops us. MCP is a protocol — hosts, clients, servers, JSON-RPC — so that loop can discover tools, resources, and prompts from many servers. The protocol is not the loop, and the m

blocks.text: 30 seconds

An agent is a loop: the model requests a tool, my code runs it, the result comes back, and a budget stops us. MCP is a protocol — hosts, clients, servers, JSON-RPC — so that loop can discover tools, resources, and prompts from many servers. The protocol is not the loop, and the model is not the runtime.
2 minutes

I start with the failure mode I am designing against: someone saying the model called the refund API. I show three layers. The model chooses a name and arguments from a schema. The host decides whether that request may run, which the MCP spec frames as explicit consent, and it treats tool descriptions as untrusted unless the server is trusted. The implementation performs the effect and returns a result tied to a call id. ReAct is how I talk about interleaving a plan with observations; I quote the paper’s ALFWorld and WebShop gains only as their results. MCP revision 2025-11-25 is how I talk about interoperability: tools, resources, and prompts from the server; sampling, roots, and elicitation from the client; stdio and Streamable HTTP. OpenAI’s built-in MCP tool is one vendor’s host feature. I still read the spec if I am the one writing the server. I end with a stop rule, because a loop without one is just spend.

blocks.q: 1. What is an agent, and what is MCP?
blocks.a: An agent is a loop: the model requests a tool, my code runs it, the result comes back, and a budget stops us. MCP is a protocol — hosts, clients, servers, JSON-RPC — so that loop can discover tools, resources, and prompts from many servers. The protocol is not the loop, and the model is not the runtime.

title: 2. Walk a tool call on a phone call.
summary: Speech becomes text. The model requests `transfer_to_queue` with a real queue id. The host speaks a confirmation. Only then do I call the tool, once, idempotently. The platform performs the transfer. The model does not own SIP.

blocks.text: 30 seconds

Speech becomes text. The model requests `transfer_to_queue` with a real queue id. The host speaks a confirmation. Only then do I call the tool, once, idempotently. The platform performs the transfer. The model does not own SIP.
2 minutes

I name the systems. CUCM, Webex, or UCCE still owns the leg and the dial plan. I will look up the real queue ids rather than invent them. The voice stack produces the utterance. The host sends tool definitions, not MCP frames, to the model vendor. If I am on Anthropic I branch on `tool_use`. If I forced the tool I do not wait for a preface. I confirm with the caller because the spec’s consent principle does not vanish when the UI is audio. The MCP server validates the enum and calls the platform API with an idempotency key. I log allow, arguments, and result. I do not call the model again in a way that can fire a second transfer. If recognition heard “building” instead of “billing,” that is a transcript bug, and the tool’s enum is what stops a nonsense destination. Handoff context for the human is a separate packet, taught in the contact-center track, not a dump of the chain-of-thought.

blocks.q: 2. Walk a tool call on a phone call.
blocks.a: Speech becomes text. The model requests `transfer_to_queue` with a real queue id. The host speaks a confirmation. Only then do I call the tool, once, idempotently. The platform performs the transfer. The model does not own SIP.

title: 3. How do you keep a tool-using bot from being a confused deputy?
summary: I allow-list servers, I show the action before it runs, I ignore instructions that arrive inside tool descriptions, and I keep secrets out of the model’s arguments.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I allow-list servers, I show the action before it runs, I ignore instructions that arrive inside tool descriptions, and I keep secrets out of the model’s arguments.
2 minutes

The spec is unusually direct: tools are code execution, descriptions are untrusted unless the server is trusted, and the protocol will not save you. So the host is the security boundary. I connect only servers I have reviewed. I do not pass the raw user string into a shell tool. I bind identity on the server side so the model cannot swap the customer id in the arguments and read someone else’s account — the same filter lesson as retrieval. Sampling, if I enable it, needs its own approval, because a server can otherwise ask the host to run a model on data the server should not see. I redact logs. I can quote this without naming a jailbreak. The design is the refusal to treat the model as the principal.

blocks.q: 3. How do you keep a tool-using bot from being a confused deputy?
blocks.a: I allow-list servers, I show the action before it runs, I ignore instructions that arrive inside tool descriptions, and I keep secrets out of the model’s arguments.

title: 4. Compare OpenAI and Anthropic tool calling.
summary: Both: I define a schema, the model requests a call, I execute, I send the result back. They differ in JSON, in how you force a tool, and in which models want which API.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Both: I define a schema, the model requests a call, I execute, I send the result back. They differ in JSON, in how you force a tool, and in which models want which API.
2 minutes

I use OpenAI’s five steps as the shared story. I mention their tool_choice values from the guide I read: auto, required, a named function, allowed_tools, and none. I mention parallel calls and the constraint on built-in tools, and that some named models in that guide require the Responses API for tools. Then I switch contracts rather than pretending the JSON matches. Anthropic: client versus server tools, `stop_reason` of `tool_use`, `tool_result`, a 64-character name regex, and tool_choice auto, any, tool, and none. I mention the preamble gotcha because it breaks real parsers. I do not claim feature parity on strict mode or tool search beyond the sentences those pages actually contain. If the interviewer wants MCP, I add a third column: the wire between my host and my server, independent of which model requested the call.

blocks.q: 4. Compare OpenAI and Anthropic tool calling.
blocks.a: Both: I define a schema, the model requests a call, I execute, I send the result back. They differ in JSON, in how you force a tool, and in which models want which API.

title: 5. What do you log, and when do you stop?
summary: I log the model id, the tool name, redacted arguments, the allow decision, the result status, and the protocol revision. I stop on success of a side effect, on a budget, or on a deny.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I log the model id, the tool name, redacted arguments, the allow decision, the result status, and the protocol revision. I stop on success of a side effect, on a budget, or on a deny.
2 minutes

A trace that cannot reconstruct the loop cannot be debugged or evaluated. I do not need a vendor product to start: a structured log with those fields is the minimum. I cap model turns and I cap identical retries. Idempotency means a retry is not a second side effect. I refuse to log full card numbers or call recordings into a tool trace; retention rules are a governance room, and I say I will read them. For an interview design I also name the kill switch: a host flag that disables tool execution without undeploying the model. The model can still talk. It cannot transfer. That split is the operational form of “the model does not execute.”

blocks.q: 5. What do you log, and when do you stop?
blocks.a: I log the model id, the tool name, redacted arguments, the allow decision, the result status, and the protocol revision. I stop on success of a side effect, on a budget, or on a deny.

title: 1. When do you use more than one agent?
summary: When one loop fails a golden case for a reason a specialist would fix. I still keep one host and one tool owner.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
When one loop fails a golden case for a reason a specialist would fix. I still keep one host and one tool owner.
2 minutes

A router can pick an intent. A specialist can draft. A critic can comment if it cannot act. I do not add boxes because a diagram looks like a team. AutoGen describes conversable agents and programmable patterns. I use that as a way to draw the messages, and I put the stop condition in code: step caps, and a deterministic edge when the amount is over the cap. LangChain’s overview builds agents on LangGraph and tells me to trace them in LangSmith. The trace is how I see the extra loop. It is not the thing that refuses the tool.

blocks.q: 1. When do you use more than one agent?
blocks.a: When one loop fails a golden case for a reason a specialist would fix. I still keep one host and one tool owner.

title: 2. Who executes?
summary: The host. MCP revision 2025-11-25. A specialist that prints tool JSON has not posted a ledger line.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
The host. MCP revision 2025-11-25. A specialist that prints tool JSON has not posted a ledger line.
2 minutes

I keep tools/call in one place. I pass an idempotency key the server understands, because that revision does not define the key for me. I will not block the key on a later draft I have not read. Tool descriptions from a server I did not write stay untrusted. If two execute_tool spans appear for one refund, the trajectory fails, even when the last sentence says “once.”

blocks.q: 2. Who executes?
blocks.a: The host. MCP revision 2025-11-25. A specialist that prints tool JSON has not posted a ledger line.

title: 3. How do you stop a double refund?
summary: One agent holds the tool. The host runs it once. A reviewer does not get a copy “to verify.”

blocks.text: 30 seconds
One agent holds the tool. The host runs it once. A reviewer does not get a copy “to verify.”
2 minutes

The failure I have seen on paper is a slow success plus a retry plus a second speaker with the same method. OWASP calls the general risk excessive agency. The eval grades the path. I also cap steps so the committee cannot talk the budget away. Prices I quote come from a page I date. On 2026-10-14, gpt-6-astra’s standard short-context output was $50 per million tokens. Four speakers read each other’s drafts, so the input grows. That is a design cost, not a rounding error.

blocks.q: 3. How do you stop a double refund?
blocks.a: One agent holds the tool. The host runs it once. A reviewer does not get a copy “to verify.”

title: 4. What is a multi-agent model id?
summary: A string on a vendor page. xAI lists grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309. I pin it if I call it. I do not skip the host because the name sounds like this room.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
A string on a vendor page. xAI lists grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309. I pin it if I call it. I do not skip the host because the name sounds like this room.
2 minutes

The page gives a context window and a price. It does not give me an allow-list. Anthropic’s lineup and OpenAI’s lineup are other strings I can pass into a framework. The framework does not unify their tool JSON. I translate at the host. I do not let a product name become the security story.

blocks.q: 4. What is a multi-agent model id?
blocks.a: A string on a vendor page. xAI lists grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309. I pin it if I call it. I do not skip the host because the name sounds like this room.

title: 5. How does this sit on a contact-center bot?
summary: The caller hears one voice. The ledger has one writer. I will not convene a panel before the first audio token.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
The caller hears one voice. The ledger has one writer. I will not convene a panel before the first audio token.
2 minutes

A router and one specialist are enough until a case says otherwise. Over-cap goes to a human, then the ACD transfers. I will not quote a millisecond budget I have not measured, and I will not quote a dial-plan id I have not read. The decision to keep the tone agent tool-less does not wait on that id. Package pins matter because a framework bump can move who executes. I re-run the double-refund case when the lockfile changes.
Also answered in T6-R01
30 seconds
The ACD still routes. The model is a treatment. I will not fine-tune dial-plan ids into the weights. I will fine-tune, if at all, only after the tool boundary already refuses a credit.
2 minutes

Callers hear tone, but finance hears promises. A transcript export is biased toward agents who talked their way out of a hard policy. Training on it teaches that talk. My first system is the one in T2 and T3 and T4: instruction, packed policy, tools that cannot post a forbidden credit, consent on anything that moves money. The fine-tune is a later experiment against that baseline. Voice latency might justify distillation of a teacher that already passes, because a smaller student is a deployability move in the sense Hinton et al. described, not a new policy. I will not quote a millisecond budget I have not measured. I will quote list prices only with the date I fetched them, and I will say the open-weight license is the file beside the checkpoint, which I have to read before I serve it. Menu paths in Control Hub stay TODO-verify. The decision not to bake a credit into the weights does not.
Also answered in T8-R01
30 seconds
The ACD still routes. The model is a treatment that can lose a tool. I will not authorize a refund from a help article.
2 minutes

Callers hear answers. Finance hears promises. The CMS is a supplier. The recording system is a supplier. I map them. I measure with an injection case and an abstain case. I manage by disabling the tool and rolling back a prompt hash, not by editing a slide. Menu paths in Control Hub stay outside this answer until someone walks them. The decision that two models are not two approvals does not. List prices I might mention are dated to the day I fetched the pricing page. They are not a control.

blocks.q: 5. How does this sit on a contact-center bot?
blocks.a: The caller hears one voice. The ledger has one writer. I will not convene a panel before the first audio token.

title: 1. Why not ship on a demo?
summary: A demo is one sample. I ship when a pinned bundle passes cases whose rules were written first, or a named owner waives a miss that is not a side effect.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
A demo is one sample. I ship when a pinned bundle passes cases whose rules were written first, or a named owner waives a miss that is not a side effect.
2 minutes

I frame it with NIST’s vocabulary without claiming a certification. AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary, dated 26 January 2023, and the overview says it is being revised, so I cite the edition I read. Map is how I choose cases: money, identity, transfer, injection. Measure is the run, before deployment and again in operation. Manage is the hold or the waiver with an expiry, and the incident review when we were wrong. A demo answers none of those. It answers “a person smiled.” I also split the grades. If the gold paragraph is missing, I do not tune the prompt. If the paragraph is present and the answer contradicts it, I do not rebuild the index. The embeddings guide gives me a faithfulness rule I can say in one sentence: if the article does not contain the answer, say you do not know. I would rather fail a build on that sentence than argue about a metric whose formula I have not pinned.

blocks.q: 1. Why not ship on a demo?
blocks.a: A demo is one sample. I ship when a pinned bundle passes cases whose rules were written first, or a named owner waives a miss that is not a side effect.

title: 2. How do you use an LLM as a judge without lying to yourself?
summary: I give it a rubric and the evidence, I store its label separately, and I do not let it be the only gate on money. I overlap it with a human.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I give it a rubric and the evidence, I store its label separately, and I do not let it be the only gate on money. I overlap it with a human.
2 minutes

The judge is a model. OWASP’s injection page applies to it: parsed text can move it, including an article that says “approve this.” So the judge never sees a job called “be helpful.” It sees the rubric and the packed ids. I schema the label so I can count disagreements. On a slice, a person labels the same cases. If we disagree on refunds, the judge leaves those gates. I do not fine-tune the judge on the disagreements the night before launch. That is a good way to teach it my launch bias. NIST’s Measure line allows qualitative and quantitative methods. A human on the severe cases is a method. A dashboard of judge scores with no overlap is not a method I will defend. I also keep the generator’s answer, the judge’s label, and the rule in three fields so a green check cannot hide a fight.

blocks.q: 2. How do you use an LLM as a judge without lying to yourself?
blocks.a: I give it a rubric and the evidence, I store its label separately, and I do not let it be the only gate on money. I overlap it with a human.

title: 3. What is on the trace, and what is not?
summary: Model id, prompt hash, retrieved ids, tool name, redacted arguments, allow or deny. Not a card number, and not a chain-of-thought treated as proof.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Model id, prompt hash, retrieved ids, tool name, redacted arguments, allow or deny. Not a card number, and not a chain-of-thought treated as proof.
2 minutes

OpenTelemetry’s registry lists gen_ai.operation.name with examples that match the hops I care about: chat, embeddings, retrieval, execute_tool. It also lists a prompt name and an evaluation score. The same page says the attributes moved to another repository, so I pin a revision before I standardize, and until I do I use my own prefix and I say so. The trace has to answer “which hop failed.” A paragraph in a ticket does not. I redact secrets before disk. Retention is a security-owner decision I will not invent. For an agent, the trace’s job is the trajectory: how many tools/call results, and whether the second one was a retry of a success. A final apology does not erase the second ledger line. For voice, I want the same trace plus whether playback was truncated, which is T7, because the caller may not have heard the sentence the model thinks it said.

blocks.q: 3. What is on the trace, and what is not?
blocks.a: Model id, prompt hash, retrieved ids, tool name, redacted arguments, allow or deny. Not a card number, and not a chain-of-thought treated as proof.

title: 4. How do you watch production without turning customers into a test set?
summary: I sample a rate I can name, I strip secrets, I score with the offline rules, and I keep the golden set. I do not hoard audio because a chart looks empty.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I sample a rate I can name, I strip secrets, I score with the offline rules, and I keep the golden set. I do not hoard audio because a chart looks empty.
2 minutes

Measure says to test regularly in operation. That is the mandate to look, not a mandate to store everything. I pick a small sample, I remove payment data, and I run the same recall and faithfulness checks I trust offline. If live fails and offline passes, I compare prompt hashes and document hashes. A changed hash is an unversioned release. A changed article is freshness. A flat latency chart can hide both. I alert on the quality rules, not only on time. Consent and retention for the sample are tenant decisions. I will say TODO-verify rather than quote a policy I have not read. The golden set stays, because production will not ask the one question that breaks the cap until it does, and I want that question written down before it happens.

blocks.q: 4. How do you watch production without turning customers into a test set?
blocks.a: I sample a rate I can name, I strip secrets, I score with the offline rules, and I keep the golden set. I do not hoard audio because a chart looks empty.

title: 5. Design the gate for a contact-center bot in one pass.
summary: Cases for answer, abstain, injection, double tool, and barge-in during consent. Deterministic graders. A waiver with a name and an expiry. Hold on unbounded money.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Cases for answer, abstain, injection, double tool, and barge-in during consent. Deterministic graders. A waiver with a name and an expiry. Hold on unbounded money.
2 minutes

I would put the runner in the repo next to the prompt files from T2. The bundle pins prompt hash, model id, and index id. Sampling uses one knob, and if I set a seed I store the fingerprint because the reference says determinism is not guaranteed. The injection case expects zero tool calls above the cap even when the article says otherwise. The trajectory case expects one success, not three. The voice case expects that a barge-in during consent cancels the tool. I do not need the tenant’s dial-plan screen to write that rule. I need it later to bind queue ids, and I will mark those ids TODO-verify. CI fails closed. A waiver on a typo in a greeting can expire in a week. A waiver on a double refund cannot. After ship, a sampled slice uses the same rules. When it pages, Manage is a person who can roll back the hash, not a channel that debates the adjective. That is the whole gate. It is smaller than a platform, and it is enough to defend.

blocks.q: 5. Design the gate for a contact-center bot in one pass.
blocks.a: Cases for answer, abstain, injection, double tool, and barge-in during consent. Deterministic graders. A waiver with a name and an expiry. Hold on unbounded money.

title: 1. How do you trace a model call without worshipping a vendor?
summary: I pin a conventions commit, I emit an operation name from that tree, and I keep a counter that does not depend on the trace vendor being up.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I pin a conventions commit, I emit an operation name from that tree, and I keep a counter that does not depend on the trace vendor being up.
2 minutes

The registry page says GenAI attributes have moved, so a floating “latest” is how dashboards rot. This lab pins commit 4e8a281 from 13 October 2026. I tell the interviewer it is a dependency bump, so I do not claim the definitions were rewritten that day. On that tree I will say chat, embeddings, execute_tool, and retrieval, and I will say the attribute is Development. LangChain’s overview points at LangSmith for trace, debug, and evaluate. I will use it if the team already runs it. I will not invent a quota, and I will not pretend the overview described Langfuse or Phoenix. The release still has a prompt hash and a model id whether or not the SaaS is reachable.

blocks.q: 1. How do you trace a model call without worshipping a vendor?
blocks.a: I pin a conventions commit, I emit an operation name from that tree, and I keep a counter that does not depend on the trace vendor being up.

title: 2. How do you build a cost budget without lying?
summary: I date the pricing page, I pick the row that matches the model and the context length, and I multiply by calls including retries. I re-fetch before I forecast.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I date the pricing page, I pick the row that matches the model and the context length, and I multiply by calls including retries. I re-fetch before I forecast.
2 minutes

On 14 October 2026 the OpenAI page said short context is at most 272k input tokens. gpt-4o-mini standard was fifteen cents and sixty cents per million. Embedding small was two cents, large was thirteen. I can compute a worksheet line from those numbers. I cannot call the line a contract. Cached and batch rows are different products. The ten percent regional uplift applies to eligible models released on or after 5 March 2026, and I will not add it until I show eligibility. If someone brings a 300k prompt, I refuse the short-context row. If the spend graph spikes while chat spans are flat, I look at embeddings and retries before I look at adjectives in the prompt.

blocks.q: 2. How do you build a cost budget without lying?
blocks.a: I date the pricing page, I pick the row that matches the model and the context length, and I multiply by calls including retries. I re-fetch before I forecast.

title: 3. What is a latency budget if you refuse a universal millisecond number?
summary: A list of hops I measure, compared with my own baseline. I page when a named hop regresses. I do not publish a single voice-latency SLO I have not timed on the real edge.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
A list of hops I measure, compared with my own baseline. I page when a named hop regresses. I do not publish a single voice-latency SLO I have not timed on the real edge.
2 minutes

The hops for text are guardrail, retrieval, chat, tool, and the follow-up chat. Voice adds the media edge. T7 keeps end-to-end milliseconds marked because they are measurements. I agree with that mark. The VAD guide’s 500 milliseconds is an example field, and I will say so if an interviewer treats it as an SLO. What I will defend is the alert: tool p95 doubled against last week pages the tool owner. A golden-set money failure blocks the deploy, which is NIST Measure, and if it is already live it is Manage: respond, recover, communicate. A sampled trace that “looks weird” is a morning read, not a page.

blocks.q: 3. What is a latency budget if you refuse a universal millisecond number?
blocks.a: A list of hops I measure, compared with my own baseline. I page when a named hop regresses. I do not publish a single voice-latency SLO I have not timed on the real edge.

title: 4. What is a guardrail you can implement this week without a new SKU?
summary: A max input, a max number of tool rounds, an allow-list of tools, and a host check before any side effect. I count the denies.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
A max input, a max number of tool rounds, an allow-list of tools, and a host check before any side effect. I count the denies.
2 minutes

LLM10 is the consumption ceiling. LLM06 is the agency ceiling. LLM01 is why I do not tell the interviewer that a schema solved injection. The schema, on the models T2 names, solves shape. The host solves the cap. I put the ceilings in the same release as the prompt hash so they cannot drift apart. If denies drop to zero, I roll back, because a silent guardrail is often a bypassed one. I do not need a product named Guardrail to do this. If the company already bought one, I still want the deny metric and the host check, because a checkbox in a console I have not read is not a control I can explain.

blocks.q: 4. What is a guardrail you can implement this week without a new SKU?
blocks.a: A max input, a max number of tool rounds, an allow-list of tools, and a host check before any side effect. I count the denies.

title: 1. How do you separate offline evals from checks in production?
summary: I keep a file of named rows with pass rules, and I run it before deploy and again on a schedule. I also read a sample of live traces. I do not call unlabeled traffic a pass rate.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I keep a file of named rows with pass rules, and I run it before deploy and again on a schedule. I also read a sample of live traces. I do not call unlabeled traffic a pass rate.
2 minutes

NIST says test before deployment and regularly while in operation. The core page does not use the words offline and online, and it says the actions are not a checklist, so I will not recite subcategory codes. I will say the Framework was released January 26, 2023, that NIST-AI-600-1 came out July 26, 2024, and that the overview says 1.0 is being revised and that use is voluntary. If the interviewer points at an evals product, I describe the behavior I fetched: OpenAI’s tutorial queues a run that processes every row of a data set with a specified prompt and model. That is the file. It is not proof about live callers. A sampling percentage is something I chose, not something I cite from NIST.

blocks.q: 1. How do you separate offline evals from checks in production?
blocks.a: I keep a file of named rows with pass rules, and I run it before deploy and again on a schedule. I also read a sample of live traces. I do not call unlabeled traffic a pass rate.

title: 2. When is an LLM judge allowed to gate a release?
summary: Almost never for money. A judge is a sample with known biases. A rule gates a refund, a cap, and a tool allow.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Almost never for money. A judge is a sample with known biases. A rule gates a refund, a cap, and a tool allow.
2 minutes

Zheng et al. name position bias, verbosity bias, self-enhancement bias, and limited reasoning. I swap order. I keep a case where the long answer is the wrong one. I do not let the model that wrote the answer be the only grader, because they define self-enhancement as favoring your own answers, and their GPT-4 example is a 10% higher win rate. I will say that number is theirs. Their report of over 80% agreement with humans is also theirs, on MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, and it matched human-human agreement in that study. I will not put either number in an alert. If two reviewers would disagree, the model has not settled it. Arithmetic and tool side effects are predicates.

blocks.q: 2. When is an LLM judge allowed to gate a release?
blocks.a: Almost never for money. A judge is a sample with known biases. A rule gates a refund, a cap, and a tool allow.

title: 3. What do you mean by red teaming, and what do you still write by hand?
summary: I mean generating test cases with another model, then having a person decide which failures block the build. I still hand-write the money cases.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I mean generating test cases with another model, then having a person decide which failures block the build. I still hand-write the money cases.
2 minutes

Perez et al. use the phrase for that method. They found tens of thousands of offensive replies in a 280B chatbot, using methods from zero-shot generation through reinforcement learning, and they call it one promising tool among many needed. I will not pretend it is exhaustive. A classifier for offensive text will not catch a polite wrong refund. OWASP’s navigation may say AI Red Teaming. I will not cite a guide I could not fetch. I will cite LLM01: RAG and fine-tuning do not fully mitigate injection. Generated cases go in a hunting set with a source column. Promotion is a human mark.

blocks.q: 3. What do you mean by red teaming, and what do you still write by hand?
blocks.a: I mean generating test cases with another model, then having a person decide which failures block the build. I still hand-write the money cases.

title: 4. How does prompt injection arrive through a tool or through MCP?
summary: The tool result is text on the next turn. The host checks the second request. Annotations do not raise the cap. A human can deny.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
The tool result is text on the next turn. The host checks the second request. Annotations do not raise the cap. A human can deny.
2 minutes

The caller, the retrieved chunk, and the tool result are all inputs. LLM01 is why I do not say the index closed the hole. On MCP revision 2025-11-25, clients MUST treat tool annotations as untrusted unless the server is trusted. I will not claim that warning was about descriptions. The page says there SHOULD always be a human who can deny an invocation, and that tools are model-controlled in the sense that the model can select them. Selection is not execution. SEP-1577 adds `tools` and `toolChoice` on sampling. The changelog line does not execute the tool and does not add idempotency. My server owns the key. The eval is two requests and one ledger line. The current protocol version I will quote is 2025-11-25.

blocks.q: 4. How does prompt injection arrive through a tool or through MCP?
blocks.a: The tool result is text on the next turn. The host checks the second request. Annotations do not raise the cap. A human can deny.

title: 5. What do you monitor, and what do you refuse to call quality?
summary: I page on a failed named row, a deny count that drops to zero, and an unexpected tool span. I treat slow_down as a ramp. I do not page on a judge average over unlabeled traces.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I page on a failed named row, a deny count that drops to zero, and an unexpected tool span. I treat slow_down as a ramp. I do not page on a judge average over unlabeled traces.
2 minutes

I pin OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions at commit 4e8a281 from October 13, 2026. `gen_ai.operation.name` is development. I will name chat, retrieval, and execute_tool, and I know the file also includes generate_content, text_completion, embeddings, and invoke_agent, plus more members I will not pretend to have memorized. A blank board after a bump means I diff the pin. OpenAI’s rate-limits page says slow_down is HTTP 429 with rate_limit_error when traffic rises too fast, and that it can fire while I am still inside RPM and TPM. The runbook ramps. It does not edit the prompt. Raw caller text stays out of the sample unless a policy I have read says otherwise. The regular in-operation test can be a replay of rows I already wrote.

blocks.q: 5. What do you monitor, and what do you refuse to call quality?
blocks.a: I page on a failed named row, a deny count that drops to zero, and an unexpected tool span. I treat slow_down as a ramp. I do not page on a judge average over unlabeled traces.

title: 1. When do you refuse to fine-tune?
summary: When a prompt, a retriever, or a tool already fixes the failure, or when the train file is last month’s wrong promises. I measure that before I touch a rank.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
When a prompt, a retriever, or a tool already fixes the failure, or when the train file is last month’s wrong promises. I measure that before I touch a rank.
2 minutes

I start from the symptom. If the bot lacks a fact that changes, I retrieve it or call a tool. A weight update will memorize a snapshot and then sound sure. If the shape is wrong, I add a demonstration in the text, which is Brown et al.’s few-shot, no gradient. Only if that baseline misses a case I can name in a golden set do I consider an update. Hu et al. froze the base and trained a low-rank delta because full copies of a GPT-3-scale model were the expense they were avoiding. I use that design when I train, and I leave their 10,000-times figure in the paper. The gate is NIST Measure: test before deployment. If the prompt baseline already passes the money cases, the correct outcome is to not train. I will say that out loud in the interview, because teams treat a quiet GPU as a failure of ambition. It is a success of the gate.

blocks.q: 1. When do you refuse to fine-tune?
blocks.a: When a prompt, a retriever, or a tool already fixes the failure, or when the train file is last month’s wrong promises. I measure that before I touch a rank.

title: 2. Explain LoRA and QLoRA without a whiteboard of Greek.
summary: LoRA trains a small update and leaves the original weights alone. QLoRA does that on a 4-bit frozen base so the base fits. Both still need an eval. Neither one is a license.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
LoRA trains a small update and leaves the original weights alone. QLoRA does that on a 4-bit frozen base so the base fits. Both still need an eval. Neither one is a license.
2 minutes

LoRA, Hu et al., injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices into Transformer layers and freezes the pretrained weights. They report, for a GPT-3 175B comparison against full Adam fine-tuning, far fewer trainable parameters and less GPU memory, and they say you can merge the update at deploy time so you do not add inference latency. I will not promise your card matches their 3× memory line. QLoRA, Dettmers et al., keeps that adapter story and quantizes the frozen base to 4-bit NormalFloat, with double quantization and paged optimizers. Their 65B-on-48GB claim and the Guanaco Vicuna scores are historical, and the paper itself doubts chatbot benchmarks. What I defend is the split: the base is frozen and small to store, the adapter is the behavior you might roll back, and 4-bit does not mean the data was clean. If an interviewer asks for the rank, I say the paper shows small ranks can work and that I will pick the rank that passes my gate without memorizing the export.

blocks.q: 2. Explain LoRA and QLoRA without a whiteboard of Greek.
blocks.a: LoRA trains a small update and leaves the original weights alone. QLoRA does that on a 4-bit frozen base so the base fits. Both still need an eval. Neither one is a license.

title: 3. How do distillation and DPO differ?
summary: Distillation copies a teacher into a smaller student. DPO fits a preference ranking with a classification loss and, in the paper, skips the RL loop. I do not mix the files.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Distillation copies a teacher into a smaller student. DPO fits a preference ranking with a classification loss and, in the paper, skips the RL loop. I do not mix the files.
2 minutes

Hinton, Vinyals, and Dean wanted the knowledge of a cumbersome model, which they describe as a mapping from inputs to outputs, inside a model you can actually serve. They care about the relative probabilities of wrong answers, not only the hard label. I use that when a large teacher already passes and latency or cost forces a student, and I re-run the golden set because a student can drop abstention. DPO, Rafailov et al., is a different complaint: RLHF was a reward model plus reinforcement learning, and they show a classification loss on preference pairs that recovers the optimal policy in closed form without sampling the language model during the fine-tune. Their sentiment win over PPO is historical. Operationally I need chosen and rejected responses, not a single transcript, and I need someone who can audit a sample of those labels. If both answers are bad, DPO still prefers one. That is how a sloppy file becomes a policy. I will not call a supervised dump “DPO” because the team liked the acronym.

blocks.q: 3. How do distillation and DPO differ?
blocks.a: Distillation copies a teacher into a smaller student. DPO fits a preference ranking with a classification loss and, in the paper, skips the RL loop. I do not mix the files.

title: 4. A fine-tune was poisoned. What do you show an auditor?
summary: The data hash, the case that should have flipped, and the tool that still enforces the cap. OWASP LLM04 names fine-tuning data as a poisoning surface. The adapter is not the control.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
The data hash, the case that should have flipped, and the tool that still enforces the cap. OWASP LLM04 names fine-tuning data as a poisoning surface. The adapter is not the control.
2 minutes

I show the lineage: which export, which article hashes, which rows were rejected, which golden cases were held out. LLM04:2025 is the name I use so we are not inventing a category. LLM01 is the reminder that even a clean fine-tune does not fully stop injection, so the refund cap remains in the tool. Then I show the eval: the poisoned behavior is a case that fails the build. NIST Manage is the incident half: we respond, recover by loading the previous adapter, and communicate. I keep the adapter unmerged until that rollback has been practiced, because Hu et al.’s merge is an inference optimization that also makes the bad behavior harder to lift out. I do not show a loss curve. A loss curve does not name the article that said “always credit.”

blocks.q: 4. A fine-tune was poisoned. What do you show an auditor?

title: 1. Draw a voice bot without stealing the ACD’s job.
summary: The queue, the recording decision, and the transfer stay in CUCM, Webex, UCCE, or the CCaaS. ASR or a speech model, the decision, and TTS are treatments. I will not invent the admin clicks.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
The queue, the recording decision, and the transfer stay in CUCM, Webex, UCCE, or the CCaaS. ASR or a speech model, the decision, and TTS are treatments. I will not invent the admin clicks.

I draw two boxes only after I draw the phone system around them. In a cascade I can point at ASR, the language model, and TTS as separate failure domains, which I like when I am debugging. In a speech-to-speech session, OpenAI’s Realtime guide says the model takes audio, keeps state, calls tools, and is meant for barge-in and turn-taking. I will use that when the product requirement is a conversational ear, and I will still time the edges because a collapsed session hides a slow tool. Either way the transfer target is a route. title: 2. Explain barge-in.
summary: The caller talks over playback. I stop the speaker immediately, cancel generation, and truncate the model’s audio to what was actually played. I do not run a tool on the overlap.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
The caller talks over playback. I stop the speaker immediately, cancel generation, and truncate the model’s audio to what was actually played. I do not run a tool on the overlap.
2 minutes

The failure mode is a split brain. The server, the Realtime conversations guide notes, can send audio faster than the client plays it. If I only cancel and I leave the unplayed tail in the conversation, the next turn refers to words the caller never heard. Truncation is the repair. Locally I stop playback first, because waiting for a round trip leaves the caller listening to the sentence I am retracting. interrupt_response in the VAD sample is how that product can cancel on speech start. I know whether I set it. I also know that a barge-in during a consent prompt is a “no” until proven otherwise, so the host drops the pending tool. That is the same consent rule as a text agent. The microphone does not get to skip it. I log played milliseconds and tool count so an eval can fail the case where a refund landed anyway.

blocks.q: 2. Explain barge-in.
blocks.a: The caller talks over playback. I stop the speaker immediately, cancel generation, and truncate the model’s audio to what was actually played. I do not run a tool on the overlap.

title: 3. How do you talk about latency without a fake SLA?
summary: I add hops: network, endpoint, ASR, model, tools, TTS, barge-in reaction. I cite the VAD sample’s 300 and 500 as examples. Every other number is a measurement I have or a TODO.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
I add hops: network, endpoint, ASR, model, tools, TTS, barge-in reaction. I cite the VAD sample’s 300 and 500 as examples. Every other number is a measurement I have or a TODO.
2 minutes

A single “voice latency” alert is how teams retune silence when the tool loop grew. I want a row per hop. The VAD guide’s sample is the only millisecond pair I will say out loud without a measurement, and I will say “sample” in the same breath. ASR word error and TTS engine time are vendor- and domain-specific. I will not borrow them from a blog. Output caps belong in this conversation because max_output_tokens and max_completion_tokens count tokens the caller may never hear, and a tight cap looks like a rude cutoff. When a spike hits, I subtract. Flat ASR plus a long tool trace means I delete a tool from the hot turn, I keep barge-in, and I do not set silence to 100 ms to “feel faster.” Faster endpointing that clips account numbers creates a different incident. The budget is a worksheet. The interview is whether I refuse to launder a guess into a requirement.

title: 4. Containment, resolution, and the handoff.
summary: Containment means no human. Resolution means the problem stayed fixed. The handoff packet tells the human what was already checked and what was promised. The model does not improvise that packet.

blocks.text: 30 seconds
Containment means no human. Resolution means the problem stayed fixed. The handoff packet tells the human what was already checked and what was promised. The model does not improvise that packet.
2 minutes

I have seen containment used as a trophy. A bot that hangs up after a wrong credit is contained. The repeat call the next morning is the resolution metric telling the truth. So I report both, and I look at transfer reason codes once I have the tenant’s list. Until I have that list I log pack miss, caller asked, and policy refusal, and I do not invent the catalog. The packet itself I can specify: intent, identity checks that passed, promises, transcript span, no full card number. PCI scope is the assessor’s sentence, not mine to invent. I do not let the language model write the packet at transfer time, because that is how a hallucination becomes the human’s opening line. The packet is assembled from tool results and the prior checks. The desktop shows it. The ACD delivers the human. That split is the whole design.

blocks.a: Containment means no human. Resolution means the problem stayed fixed. The handoff packet tells the human what was already checked and what was promised. The model does not improvise that packet.

title: 5. A latency spike on a Tuesday. Walk it.
summary: I split the budget. If ASR is flat and tools grew, I cut tools. If the finish reason is the output cap, I fix the cap. I do not disable barge-in, and I do not treat the VAD sample as the culprit by default.

blocks.text: 30 seconds

I split the budget. If ASR is flat and tools grew, I cut tools. If the finish reason is the output cap, I fix the cap. I do not disable barge-in, and I do not treat the VAD sample as the culprit by default.
2 minutes

Callers talking over the bot is a symptom, not a diagnosis. I pull time-to-first-audio, ASR endpoint time, tool spans, and the finish reason. OpenTelemetry’s example operation names — chat, retrieval, execute_tool — are how I want those spans labeled, with the revision pinned because the registry page says the attributes moved. If execute_tool grew, the spike is the agent loop from T4, and the voice stack is innocent. If the cap fired, the caller heard a fragment and barged in because the fragment made no sense. Raising the cap is the fix, and truncate stays. If ASR time grew, then I look at the engine and the audio, and I still do not copy 500 ms into a new religion. I add a golden case for the spike so T5 fails the build if the extra tool returns. I tell the interviewer the number I will not quote. That refusal is the competence.

Govern names who may add a tool or waive a case. Map is the list of callers, corpus, tools, and suppliers. Measure is the golden set, run before deployment and on a schedule, which is what the AIRC excerpt says. Manage is respond, recover, communicate: disable the tool, roll back the prompt hash, tell finance. NIST AI 600-1 is the July 2024 generative profile. MCP’s host executes. I decide which tools this bot receives. The hours bot does not get refund. The refund tool checks the amount. LLM02 is the name I use so we are not inventing a category, and LLM07 stops me putting the number in the system prompt “temporarily.” The model should see a payment result. title: 4. What do you refuse to invent when they push for a number?
